norms.heading: Petition, how served.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: The petition of defendant shall be served on the plaintiff in the judgment or notice given by publication to him, or, if the plaintiff be dead, then on or to his legal representatives, in like time and manner as provided for the service or giving of notice in case of an original petition upon a defendant.

norms.heading: If answer or motion filed, cause to proceed.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: If the answer or motion is filed within the time so limited, the cause shall proceed as it would have done had the defendant appeared to the summons and filed his answer or motion to the petition; if not, the judgment shall be made absolute.

correspondences.note_fr: L'opposition permet au défaillant de faire rétracter un jugement rendu par défaut. La Rule 74.05 et les §§ 511.170, 511.200 et 511.220 prévoient des mécanismes de remise en cause d'un jugement par défaut, mais avec des conditions, délais et fondements différents.
correspondences.note_en: Opposition allows the defaulting party to obtain retraction of a default judgment. Rule 74.05 and §§ 511.170, 511.200, and 511.220 provide mechanisms to challenge default judgments, but impose different conditions, time limits, and grounds.

correspondences.note_fr: L'opposition saisit le même juge afin qu'il statue à nouveau en fait et en droit, le jugement initial ne disparaissant qu'en cas de rétractation. Les textes du Missouri permettent de faire annuler ou réexaminer le jugement par défaut et, selon le § 511.220, de reprendre l'instance comme si le défendeur avait comparu, sans reprendre exactement cette règle.
correspondences.note_en: Opposition returns the matter to the same judge for a new decision on fact and law, with the original judgment surviving unless retracted. Missouri provisions permit default-judgment relief and, under § 511.220, continuation as if the defendant had appeared, but do not reproduce the rule exactly.

correspondences.note_fr: L’affaire doit être instruite et jugée selon les règles applicables devant la juridiction ayant rendu la décision. RSMo 511.220 prévoit que, si la réponse ou la motion est déposée, la cause suit la procédure qu’elle aurait suivie si le défendeur avait comparu.
correspondences.note_en: The matter is heard and decided under the rules applicable before the court that rendered the decision. RSMo 511.220 provides that, upon timely filing of an answer or motion, the case proceeds as it would have if the defendant had appeared.

correspondences.note_fr: Après opposition, l’instance reprend comme si le défendeur avait comparu et présenté sa réponse ou sa motion. Le texte du Missouri ne précise toutefois pas que la recevabilité des prétentions doit être appréciée par référence à la demande primitive.
correspondences.note_en: After opposition, the case proceeds as if the defendant had appeared and filed an answer or motion. The Missouri text does not specify that the parties’ claims must be assessed by reference to the original claim.

norms.heading: Judgment for defendant to be what.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: If, upon the trial of a cause, judgment shall be for the defendant, or if the judgment be for the plaintiff, but for less than the original judgment, the defendant may also have judgment with costs against the plaintiff for such damages as justice shall require, as will reimburse him for moneys applied to the satisfaction of the original judgment and legal interest thereon, and which the plaintiff did not finally recover.

norms.heading: Sale of property to innocent purchaser not affected by vacating judgment.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: No sale or conveyance of property for the satisfaction of any judgment, regularly made, shall be affected or prejudiced by the setting aside any judgment on the appearance of a defendant, as herein provided, if the property shall be in the hands of innocent purchasers.

norms.heading: Motion to set aside judgment must be filed within three years.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: Judgments in any court of record shall not be set aside for irregularity, on motion, unless such motion be made within three years after the term at which such judgment was rendered.

norms.heading: Imperfections for which judgment will not be reversed or affected.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

correspondences.note_fr: L’article sanctionne par la nullité certaines irrégularités formelles du jugement et prévoit une limitation temporelle pour certaines objections. Les textes du Missouri traitent des imperfections du jugement, de leur correction et des conditions formelles d’entrée du jugement, mais leurs effets et mécanismes diffèrent.
correspondences.note_en: The article makes specified formal defects in a judgment grounds for nullity and limits the timing of certain objections. Missouri provisions address judgment imperfections, their correction, and formal entry requirements, but use different mechanisms and effects.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article écarte la nullité d’un jugement malgré l’omission ou l’inexactitude d’une mention si la régularité est établie autrement. Le Missouri neutralise également de nombreux défauts ou omissions sans préjudice et prévoit leur correction, mais selon un régime plus large et différent.
correspondences.note_en: The article prevents nullity for an omitted or inaccurate formal statement when regularity is otherwise established. Missouri likewise disregards numerous defects or omissions absent prejudice and allows their amendment, but under a broader and materially different scheme.

norms.heading: Imperfections cured by amendment.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: The omissions, imperfections, defects and variances in section 511.260 enumerated, and all others of a like nature, not being against the right and justice of the matter of the suit, and not altering the issues between the parties on the trial, shall be supplied and amended by the court where the judgment shall be given, or by the court into which such judgment shall be removed by writ of error or by appeal.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 121 écarte le prononcé d’une nullité susceptible d’être couverte lorsque sa cause a disparu au moment où le juge statue. RSMo 506.190, Rule 55.33, RSMo 511.270 et Rule 57.07 organisent diverses corrections ou cures d’irrégularités, mais dans des domaines et selon des conditions différentes.
correspondences.note_en: Article 121 prevents a curable nullity from being pronounced when its cause has disappeared by the time of decision. RSMo 506.190, Rule 55.33, RSMo 511.270, and Rule 57.07 provide various mechanisms for correcting or curing irregularities, but in narrower contexts and under different conditions.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article sanctionne par la nullité certaines irrégularités formelles du jugement et prévoit une limitation temporelle pour certaines objections. Les textes du Missouri traitent des imperfections du jugement, de leur correction et des conditions formelles d’entrée du jugement, mais leurs effets et mécanismes diffèrent.
correspondences.note_en: The article makes specified formal defects in a judgment grounds for nullity and limits the timing of certain objections. Missouri provisions address judgment imperfections, their correction, and formal entry requirements, but use different mechanisms and effects.

Le Missouri neutralise également de nombreux défauts ou omissions sans préjudice et prévoit leur correction, mais selon un régime plus large et différent.
correspondences.note_en: The article prevents nullity for an omitted or inaccurate formal statement when regularity is otherwise established. Missouri likewise disregards numerous defects or omissions absent prejudice and allows their amendment, but under a broader and materially different scheme.

norms.heading: Specific performance of judgment.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: In all cases where judgment is given for the conveyance of real estate or the delivery of personal property, the court may, by such judgment, pass the title of such property, without any act to be done on the part of the defendant.

norms.heading: Issuance of writs of possession by court.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: The court may issue a writ of possession, if necessary, to the sheriff of the proper county, to put the party entitled into possession of such real or personal property, or may proceed by attachment or sequestration.

norms.heading: Effect of judgment for conveyance.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: When an unconditional judgment shall be made for a conveyance, release or acquittance, and the party required to execute the same shall not comply therewith, such judgment shall be considered and taken to have the same operation and effect and be as available as if the conveyance, release or acquittance had been executed conformably to the judgment.

norms.heading: Damages in lieu of performance of judgment.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: When complete justice cannot otherwise be done, the court may, on the petition of the party entitled to the benefit of a final judgment, cause an inquiry to be made by a jury of the amount of damages which ought to be paid in lieu of the performance of the judgment, and may render a judgment for the damages so assessed, and award execution thereon.

norms.heading: Copy of judgment decreeing conveyance recorded — effect of failure to record.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text:
1. In all cases where any court of record shall render final judgment, adjudging or decreeing a conveyance of real estate, or that any real estate pass, or shall render any final judgment quieting or determining the title to any real estate, the party in whose favor the judgment or decree is rendered shall cause a copy thereof to be recorded in the office of the recorder of the county wherein the lands passed or to be conveyed or the title to which is quieted or determined lie, within eight months after such judgment or decree is entered.

2. If such judgment or decree be not so recorded, it shall not be valid, except between the parties thereto and such as have actual notice thereof, and in all cases in which any defendant in any such judgment or decree shall have the right, by petition for review, to show good cause for setting aside such judgment or decree, within three years after such judgment or decree is rendered, and a copy of such judgment or decree is not filed for record within eight months as herein provided, such defendant shall be allowed two years and four months from the date of the filing of a copy of such judgment or decree for record in which to file such petition for review; provided, that nothing in this section shall be construed to affect the provisions of section 511.180.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 506 autorise les formalités de publicité ou de radiation sur production d’une expédition ou copie certifiée du jugement et, si nécessaire, de la preuve de son caractère exécutoire. RSMo 511.320 et 511.450 concernent l’enregistrement ou la transcription de jugements, sans reprendre ces conditions générales.
correspondences.note_en: Article 506 permits recording, cancellation, or related entries upon production of a judgment copy and, when necessary, proof that it is enforceable. RSMo 511.320 and 511.450 concern recording or docketing judgments, but do not establish the same general conditions.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1303 fait courir le délai de publicité foncière de l’acte de changement de régime matrimonial à compter de la force de chose jugée de la décision d’homologation. Le RSMo 511.320 prévoit également un délai de publicité foncière, mais pour les jugements relatifs à la transmission ou au titre d’un immeuble, avec un délai et des effets différents.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1303 starts the land-recording period for the matrimonial-regime-change instrument when the homologation decision becomes final. RSMo 511.320 likewise imposes a recording period for judgments concerning conveyance or title to real estate, but involves a different type of judgment and different timing and effects.

norms.heading: Exceptions to section 511.320.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: Nothing contained in section 511.320 shall be so construed as to require a party to record a judgment or decree when a conveyance has been executed in pursuance thereof, and acknowledged or proved and deposited for record in the proper office within the time therein limited.

norms.heading: Performance of judgment, enforcement.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: When a judgment requires the performance of any other act than the payment of money, a certified copy of the judgment may be served upon the party against whom it is given, and his obedience thereto required. If he neglect or refuse, he may be punished by the court as for a contempt, by fine or imprisonment, or both, and, if necessary, by sequestration of property.
revisor_notes: (1976) Where circuit court reversed and held for naught the impeachment proceedings of city removing the city marshal, the city could not be held in contempt for failure to take affirmative action such as paying the marshal's salary and emoluments due during the period of suspension where these acts were not required specifically in the original judgment. State ex rel. City of Pacific v. Buford (A.), 534 S.W.2d 819.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article exige, en principe, une expédition revêtue de la formule exécutoire pour mettre un jugement ou un acte à exécution. Le Missouri autorise l’exécution au profit de la partie gagnante et prévoit une demande d’exécution, mais ne reprend pas cette exigence formelle générale ; une copie certifiée est prévue pour certains jugements non pécuniaires.
correspondences.note_en: The article generally requires an enforceable certified copy bearing the enforcement clause before execution. Missouri allows the prevailing party to obtain execution and requires an application, while a certified copy is specified only for certain non-money judgments; it has no general equivalent to the enforcement-clause requirement.

correspondences.note_fr: L’exécution contre le débiteur suppose la notification préalable du jugement, sauf exécution volontaire, avec une règle particulière pour l’exécution au seul vu de la minute. Le Missouri prévoit la signification d’une copie certifiée pour certains actes non pécuniaires et un avis spécial dans certaines ventes immobilières, mais pas une règle générale identique.
correspondences.note_en: Execution against the debtor generally requires prior notice of the judgment, unless performance is voluntary, with a special rule for execution on presentation of the original. Missouri requires service of a certified copy for certain non-money judgments and special notice in some real-estate executions, but has no identical general rule.

norms.heading: Liens on real estate established by judgment or decrees in courts of record, exception — associate circuit court, procedure required — no administrative amendments.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text:
1. Judgments and decrees entered by the supreme court, by any United States district or circuit court held within this state, by any district of the court of appeals, by any circuit court and any probate division of the circuit court, except judgments and decrees rendered by associate, small claims and municipal divisions of the circuit courts, shall be liens on the real estate of the person against whom they are entered, situate in the county for which or in which the court is held.

2. Judgments and decrees rendered by the associate divisions of the circuit courts shall not be liens on the real estate of the person against whom they are rendered until such judgments or decrees are filed with the clerk of the circuit court pursuant to sections 517.141 and 517.151.

3. Judgments and decrees entered by the small claims and municipal divisions of the circuit court shall not constitute liens against the real estate of the person against whom they are rendered.

4. Notwithstanding any other provision of law, no judgments or decrees entered by any court of competent jurisdiction may be amended or modified by any administrative agency without the approval of a court of competent jurisdiction.

5. Notwithstanding subsection 4 of this section or any other law to the contrary, no judgments or decrees entered by any court of competent jurisdiction relating to child support orders may be amended or modified by any administrative agency without the approval of a court of competent jurisdiction.

norms.heading: Commencement, extent and duration of lien — applicability of duration of lien.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: The lien of a judgment or decree shall extend as well to the real estate acquired after the rendition thereof, as to that which was owned when the judgment or decree was rendered. Such liens shall commence on the day of the rendition of the judgment, and shall continue for ten years, subject to be revived as herein provided; but when two or more judgments or decrees are rendered at the same term, as between the parties entitled to such judgments or decrees, the lien shall commence on the last day of the term at which they are rendered. The provisions of this section relating to the duration of the lien on real estate shall apply only to judgments or decrees rendered or revived after August 28, 1998, and, for all judgments or decrees entered prior to such date, the lien of such judgment or decree shall continue for three years from the date such lien commenced.

norms.heading: Scire facias to revive, may issue, when.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: The plaintiff or his legal representative may, at any time within ten years, sue out a scire facias to revive a judgment and lien; but after the expiration of ten years from the rendition of the judgment, no scire facias shall issue.

norms.heading: Revival to take effect from rendition.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: If a scire facias be issued after the expiration of the lien, and a judgment of revival is afterward rendered, such revival shall only take effect from the rendition thereof, and shall not prevail over intermediate encumbrances.

norms.heading: Scire facias before lien expires, effect of.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: If a scire facias is issued to revive a judgment and lien before the expiration of the lien, and a judgment of revival is afterward rendered, although it may be after the expiration of the lien, yet the said lien shall prevail over all intermediate encumbrances.

norms.heading: Scire facias, how served and when triable.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: The scire facias shall be served on the defendant or his legal representatives, terre tenants or other persons occupying the land, and be directed to and executed in any county in this state. All such cases shall be tried at the return term, except they are continued for cause.

norms.heading: Publication ordered, when.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: If the defendant cannot be found, the court may make an order setting forth briefly the nature of the case, and requiring all persons interested to show cause, at the next term of such court, why such judgment or decree should not be revived and the lien continued.

norms.heading: Publication of order.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: The order shall be published in some newspaper printed in this state for three weeks, the last insertion to be two weeks before the commencement of the term at which the parties are required to appear.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article prévoit la publication du jugement rejetant la demande de séparation de biens, par renvoi aux modalités de l’article 1292. RSMo 511.420 prévoit aussi la publication d’un ordre judiciaire pendant une période déterminée, mais dans un contexte procédural différent et sans viser ce jugement matrimonial.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires publication of a judgment rejecting judicial separation of property. RSMo 511.420 also requires publication of a court order for a specified period, but in a different procedural setting and without addressing this matrimonial judgment.

norms.heading: Judgment of revival, when.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: If upon the service of the scire facias or publication as aforesaid, the defendant, or any of his creditors, do not appear and show cause against reviving the judgment or decree, the same shall be revived, and the lien continued for another period of three years; and so on, from time to time, as often as may be necessary.

norms.heading: Transcript of judgment a lien in another county, when — procedure.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text:
1. Judgments and decrees obtained in the supreme court or any district of the court of appeals or any United States court or any court of record in this state shall, upon the filing of a transcript thereof in the office of the clerk of the circuit court of any other county and indexing of such transcript as provided in subsection 2 of this section, be a lien upon the real estate of the person against whom such judgment or decree is rendered, situate in the county in which such transcript is filed.

2. Such judgment or decree as provided in subsection 1 of this section shall be entered in the record kept by the clerk of the circuit court having jurisdiction of civil causes within a county or a city not within a county, for judgments and decrees of the circuit court of such county as provided in section 511.500, except that the record of entry of such judgment or decree shall also include the name and location of the court that rendered such judgment or decree.

norms.heading: Judgment docketed and recorded, when.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: As soon as such transcript shall be filed in the office of the clerk of the circuit court of any county, the clerk thereof shall forthwith enter the judgment or decree in the judgment docket of said court, in the same manner as is provided for entering judgments rendered in such court; and the clerk shall also record such transcript in a record to be kept for that purpose, and shall record, both in the judgment docket and upon the record of such transcript, the time of filing the same in his office.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 506 autorise les formalités de publicité ou de radiation sur production d’une expédition ou copie certifiée du jugement et, si nécessaire, de la preuve de son caractère exécutoire. RSMo 511.320 et 511.450 concernent l’enregistrement ou la transcription de jugements, sans reprendre ces conditions générales.
correspondences.note_en: Article 506 permits recording, cancellation, or related entries upon production of a judgment copy and, when necessary, proof that it is enforceable. RSMo 511.320 and 511.450 concern recording or docketing judgments, but do not establish the same general conditions.

norms.heading: Such liens to have the force of other judgment liens.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: The lien created by sections 511.440 to 511.480 shall exist to the same extent and for the same time only as the lien of the judgment or decree in the county where the same was rendered; and a transcript of a judgment or decree reviving a judgment or decree, or the lien thereof, may be filed, docketed and recorded in the same manner and with like effect as an original judgment or decree.

norms.heading: Execution and revival sued out where judgment was rendered — except magistrate judgments.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text:
1. Sections 511.460 to 511.480 shall be deemed to authorize the court where such transcript shall be filed to issue executions on such judgment or decree and to exercise all powers incident to the judgment including judgment debtor proceedings, and a scire facias to revive such judgment or decree or lien.

2. Transcripts of judgments described in section 511.440 shall not authorize the courts where such transcripts shall be filed to issue executions thereon or to issue a scire facias to revive such judgments, but they shall issue and be sued out of the court where the original judgment or decree was rendered.

norms.heading: Clerk — failure to perform duty — penalty.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: Any clerk of a court who shall refuse or neglect, after tender of his fees for the same, to file and record such transcript and docket such judgment or decree, as in sections 511.440 to 511.480 directed, shall be liable on his official bond to any person damaged by reason of such refusal or neglect, in double the amount of damages sustained.

norms.heading: Abstract of judgment filed with circuit clerk to establish lien on real property — priority of liens (counties and City of St. Louis).

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: No judgment hereafter rendered by any court shall be a lien on real estate situate in such counties or city not within a county, until an abstract of the judgment shall be entered in a record prepared and maintained in the manner prescribed by supreme court rule which shall be available for public inspection in the office of the circuit clerk, and which shall state: the names of the parties; the date of the judgment; the nature of the judgment or decree; the amount of the debt, damages and costs; and the satisfaction or other disposition thereof, with any necessary notes thereon. The liens of all judgments entered in such record, as provided in this section, shall have priority according to the sequence of and from the time of its respective entry into the record, such time being deemed within the period of time in which the abstract thereof should be furnished to or provided by the circuit clerk pursuant to the provisions of this chapter.

norms.heading: Duty of clerk to furnish and enter abstracts — satisfaction of judgments — liability of clerk.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: It shall be the duty of the clerks of any division of the circuit court to, within five days after the rendition of any final judgment in their respective division, enter an abstract of such judgment in the record as required in section 511.500; and the clerk shall immediately enter the same when the abstract aforesaid shall be furnished to such clerk by any party interested, or such party's agent; and each of the clerks and their sureties shall be respectively liable for any damage occasioned by any neglect to perform the duties hereby required of them respectively; and it is further provided that whenever any personal representative, guardian or conservator, or any party interested, or such party's agent, shall exhibit to the clerk of the court wherein such judgment may be recorded a receipt or certificate of the proper officer, stating that such judgment has been duly satisfied, then the circuit clerk shall, without further fee, enter satisfaction of such judgment in such clerk's office in the record as required in section 511.500.

norms.heading: Lien of judgment rendered by district No. 2 of Marion County circuit court.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: The lien of the judgment of district number 2 of the circuit court of Marion County shall be the same as the lien of the judgments of district number 1 of the circuit court for the county of Marion, and shall be governed by the same laws.

norms.heading: Death of a plaintiff, survival of judgment.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: If one or more plaintiffs in a judgment or decree shall die before the same is satisfied or carried into effect, the judgment or decree, if concerning the personalty, shall survive to the executors or administrators of such deceased party, and if concerning real estate, to his or their heirs or devisees; and execution may be sued out in the name of the surviving plaintiff or plaintiffs, or legal representatives of the deceased plaintiff, for the benefit of himself or themselves, and the legal representatives of the deceased party; or the judgment or decree may be revived in the name of such legal representatives and the surviving plaintiffs, and execution sued out by them jointly.

norms.heading: Death of a defendant, survival of judgment.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: When there are several defendants in a judgment or decree, and some of them die before the same is satisfied or carried into effect, the judgment or decree, if concerning real estate, shall survive against his or their heirs or devisees, and execution may issue against any surviving defendant or defendants, or such judgment or decree may be revived against the heirs or devisees of any or all such deceased defendants, by scire facias, and execution may be sued out against the surviving defendant or defendants, and the heirs or devisees of such deceased defendants, or such of them as are made parties jointly; but if such judgment or decree concern the personalty, execution shall be sued out only against the surviving defendant or defendants; and if the lien of the judgment or decree has not expired, it shall be exhibited in the probate division of the circuit court for allowance, as other demands against the deceased defendant or defendant's estate, but if the lien has expired, the judgment or decree shall be revived against the executors or administrators of the deceased defendant or defendants, and then shall be proceeded with as herein directed.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article permet de notifier le recours au domicile du défunt et collectivement à ses héritiers, mais exige que chacun soit cité avant qu’un jugement puisse être requis contre eux. Le Missouri prévoit la notification malgré le décès, la substitution et, dans certains cas, la poursuite ou la reprise du jugement contre les héritiers, sans reprendre exactement cette procédure.
correspondences.note_en: The article permits notice of an appeal at the deceased party’s domicile and collectively to heirs, but requires each heir to be summoned before judgment may be sought against them. Missouri addresses notice despite death, substitution, and in some cases continuation or revival against heirs, but not through the same procedure.

norms.heading: Judgment revived by or against administrator de bonis non.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: If an executor or administrator be plaintiff or defendant in a judgment or decree, and shall die, resign or be dismissed before the same is satisfied or carried into effect, the judgment or decree may be revived by or against the administrator de bonis non, in the manner aforesaid.

norms.heading: Satisfaction of judgment.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: When any judgment or decree is satisfied otherwise than by execution, the party in whose favor the same was rendered shall, immediately thereafter, enter an acknowledgment of satisfaction thereof in the court where the same was obtained, or before the clerk of such court in vacation.

norms.heading: Who may enter satisfaction.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: Satisfaction may be entered by the plaintiff in person, by his attorney of record, or by his agent duly authorized, in writing, under the hand of the plaintiff.

norms.heading: Satisfaction, where entered.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: If the acknowledgment is made in court, it shall be entered of record; but if made before the clerk in vacation, it shall be entered on the minutes, signed by the party making it, and attested by the clerk.

norms.heading: When made by agent, his authority to be filed.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: When made by an agent, his authority shall be filed in the office of the clerk of the court where the acknowledgment is made.

norms.heading: Effect of acknowledgment.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: The acknowledgment so made shall forever discharge and release the judgment or decree.

norms.heading: Refusal of party to satisfy — proceedings.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.heading: Clerks shall keep book for docketing judgments.

Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: The clerks of courts of record shall keep in their respective offices a well-bound book for entering therein an alphabetical docket of all judgments and decrees.

norms.text: They shall, during every term, or within thirty days thereafter, enter in such docket all final judgments and decrees rendered at such term in alphabetical order, by the name of the person against whom the judgment or decree was entered; and if the judgment or decree be against several persons, it shall be docketed in the name of each person against whom it was recovered, in the alphabetical order of their names, respectively.

correspondences.note_en: The judge resolves implementation difficulties and records the decision by docket notation, order, or judgment. Rule 74.01 addresses judgments or decrees and their entry, while RSMo 511.650 specifies docket entries; neither governs handwriting verification itself.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 454 énumère les mentions obligatoires du jugement, notamment la juridiction, les juges, la date, le greffier et les parties. RSMo 511.650 impose certaines mentions au docket, tandis que la Rule 74.01 définit les conditions formelles d’entrée du jugement, sans reprendre l’ensemble des mentions françaises.

norms.text: The clerks of courts of record, in recording judgments or decrees, shall leave a space or margin on the record for entering a memorandum of the satisfaction or vacation of such judgment or decree.

norms.heading: Clerk to enter disposition of judgments.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: When satisfaction of a judgment or decree shall be acknowledged or entered by order of the court, or satisfaction shall be made by execution, or such judgment or decree shall be vacated, the clerk shall enter upon the margin of the judgment or decree a memorandum of the disposition thereof, the date, and the book and page in which the evidence is entered or recorded.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1060 impose une mention marginale indiquant la radiation des mentions antérieures lorsque certaines décisions mettent fin ou rejettent une mesure inscrite au répertoire civil. Le RSMo 511.670 prévoit également une inscription marginale de la disposition d’un jugement, mais sans le mécanisme spécifique de radiation du répertoire civil.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1060 requires a marginal notation stating that certain judgments result in cancellation of earlier civil-register entries. RSMo 511.670 likewise requires a marginal entry recording the disposition of a judgment, but it does not provide the specific civil-register cancellation mechanism.

norms.heading: Failure of clerk to perform duty — penalty.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: Any clerk failing to comply with the provisions of sections 511.630 to 511.670, or who shall fail to enter in said docket, within the time required, the judgments of associate circuit judges' courts, transcripts of which have been filed in his office, shall forfeit and pay to the party injured thereby the sum of one hundred dollars, to be recovered by civil action.

norms.heading: Assignment of judgments.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: Judgments of courts of record for the recovery of money may be assigned, in writing, by the plaintiff and the assignees thereof, successively, which assignment shall be on or attached to the judgment, and attested by the clerk of the court or associate circuit judge, and, when so made and attested, shall vest the title to such judgment in each assignee thereof, successively.

norms.heading: Payment to assignor, when valid.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: Payments or satisfaction on such judgment to the assignor shall be valid, if made before notice of assignment to the judgment debtor, but not otherwise.

norms.heading: Execution on assigned judgment, how issued.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: In case of assignment, execution shall issue in the name of the original plaintiff, but shall be endorsed by the clerk or associate circuit judge to be for the use of the assignee.

norms.heading: Assignee to have right of action.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: Any action or other proceeding, which the plaintiff in any judgment might have thereon, may be maintained in the name of the assignee.

norms.heading: Execution of delivery bond to plaintiff's judgment.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: Bonds for the delivery of property levied upon by virtue of such executions shall be to the judgment plaintiff for the use of such assignee; and all suits and proceedings relating to such judgment, or against any officer on his bond, for neglect of duty relating thereto, may be against or upon the complaint of such assignee, as the case may require.

norms.heading: Submitting a controversy without action.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: Parties to a question in difference, which might be the subject of a civil action, may, without action, agree upon a case containing the facts upon which the controversy depends, and present a submission of the same to any court which would have jurisdiction if an action had been brought; but it must appear, by affidavit, that the controversy is real and the proceedings in good faith, to determine the rights of the parties; the court shall thereupon hear and determine the case, and render judgment thereon, as if an action were depending.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article pose le régime général de l’accord amiable : formation par échange des consentements, écrit et éventuelle force exécutoire. La Rule 88.08 et les RSMo 452.325 et 511.740-511.750 prévoient des accords écrits ou des soumissions et leur exécution, mais dans des cadres plus spécifiques.
correspondences.note_en: The article establishes a general regime for amicable agreements: formation by consent, possible written form, and enforceability. Rule 88.08 and RSMo 452.325 and 511.740-511.750 address written settlements or submissions and enforcement, but only in more specific settings.

correspondences.note_fr: L’homologation est demandée par requête par les parties ou la plus diligente devant le juge compétent, avec décision en principe sans débat. RSMo 513.617 et 507.184 exigent l’approbation judiciaire de certains règlements, mais dans des matières particulières; RSMo 511.740 prévoit une soumission consensuelle au tribunal, avec audition obligatoire.
correspondences.note_en: The article permits the parties, or the more diligent party, to request approval before the seized or otherwise competent judge, normally without a hearing. RSMo 513.617 and 507.184 require court approval of specified settlements, while RSMo 511.740 allows consensual submission to a competent court but requires a hearing.

norms.heading: Enforcement of judgment.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: The judgment may be enforced in the same manner as if it had been rendered in an action, unless otherwise provided in the submission; and, in like manner, shall be with costs, and subject to an appeal or writ of error, unless otherwise provided in the submission.

correspondences.note_fr: L’acquiescement au jugement implique soumission à ses chefs et renonciation aux recours, sous réserve du recours régulier d’une autre partie. Les textes du Missouri régissent le droit d’appel, le dépôt de l’avis d’appel et l’appel incident, mais ne consacrent pas expressément une renonciation par acquiescement.
correspondences.note_en: Acquiescence to a judgment entails submission to its provisions and waiver of appellate remedies, subject to another party’s timely appeal. The Missouri provisions govern the right to appeal, notices, and cross-appeals, but do not expressly create waiver by acquiescence.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article confère à la sentence l’autorité de la chose jugée, permet l’exécution provisoire et prévoit sa notification. Le Missouri définit le jugement, prévoit l’exécution d’une sentence soumise à arbitrage et règle la notification et la signification des jugements et actes, mais les textes fournis ne prévoient pas l’exécution provisoire.
correspondences.note_en: The article gives the arbitral award res judicata effect, permits provisional enforcement, and requires notice. Missouri defines a judgment, addresses enforcement of an award submitted to arbitration, and governs notice and service of judgments and papers, but the supplied texts do not provide for provisional enforcement.

norms.heading: Uniform enforcement of foreign judgments law.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text:
1. The following terms as used in this section shall mean:

(1) "Foreign judgment", any judgment, decree or order of a court of the United States or of any state or territory which is entitled to full faith and credit in this state;

(2) "Judgment debtor", the party against whom a foreign judgment has been rendered;

(3) "Levy", to take control of or create a lien upon property under any judicial writ or process whereby satisfaction of a judgment may be enforced against such property;

(4) "Register", to file and record a foreign judgment in a court of this state.

2. On application made within the time allowed for bringing an action on a foreign judgment in this state, any person entitled to bring such action may have a foreign judgment registered in any court of this state having jurisdiction in such action.

3. A verified petition for registration shall set forth a copy of the judgment to be registered, the date of its entry and the record of any subsequent entries affecting it, all authenticated in the manner authorized by the laws of the United States or of this state, and a prayer that the judgment be registered. The clerk of the registering court shall notify the clerk of the court which rendered the original judgment that application for registration has been made, and shall request him to file this information with the judgment.

4. At any time after registration the petitioner shall be entitled to have summons issued and served upon the judgment debtor as in an action brought upon the foreign judgment, in any manner authorized by the law of this state for obtaining jurisdiction of the person.

5. If jurisdiction of the person of the judgment debtor cannot be obtained, a notice clearly designating the foreign judgment and reciting the fact of registration, the court in which it is registered, and the time allowed for pleading, shall be sent by the clerk of the registering court by registered mail to the last known address of the judgment debtor. Proof of such mailing shall be made by the certificate of the clerk.

6. At any time after the registration and regardless of whether jurisdiction of the person of the judgment debtor has been secured or final judgment has been obtained, a levy may be made under the registered judgment upon any property of the judgment debtor which is subject to execution or other judicial process for satisfaction of judgments.

7. If the judgment debtor fails to plead within thirty days after jurisdiction over his person has been obtained, or if the court after hearing has refused to set the registration aside, the registered judgment shall become a final personal judgment of the court in which it is registered.

8. Any defense, setoff or counterclaim which under the law of this state may be asserted by the defendant in an action on the foreign judgment, may be presented by appropriate pleadings and the issues raised thereby shall be tried and determined as in other civil actions. Such pleadings must be filed within thirty days after personal jurisdiction is acquired or within thirty-five days after the mailing of the notice prescribed in subsection 5.

9. If the judgment debtor shows that an appeal from the original judgment is pending or that he is entitled to, and intends to appeal therefrom, the court shall, on such terms as it deems just, postpone the trial for such time as appears sufficient for the appeal to be concluded, and may set aside the levy upon proof that the defendant has furnished adequate security for satisfaction of the judgment.

10. An order setting aside a registration constitutes a final judgment in favor of the judgment debtor.

11. An appeal may be taken by either party from judgment or order sustaining or setting aside a registration on the same terms as an appeal from a judgment or order of the same court.

12. If personal jurisdiction of the judgment debtor is not secured within thirty days after the levy and he has not, within thirty-five days after the mailing of the notice prescribed by subsection 5, acted to set aside the registration or to assert a setoff or counterclaim the registered judgment shall be a final judgment quasi in rem of the court in which it is registered, binding upon the judgment debtor's interest in property levied upon, and the court shall enter an order to that effect.

13. Sale under the levy may be held at any time after final judgment, either personal or quasi in rem, but not earlier except as otherwise provided by law for sale under levy on perishable goods. Sale and distribution of the proceeds shall be made in accordance with the laws of this state.

14. When a registered foreign judgment becomes a final judgment of this state, the court shall include as part of the judgment interest payable on the foreign judgment under the law of the state in which it was rendered, and the cost of obtaining the authenticated copy of the original judgment. The court shall include as part of its judgment court costs incidental to the proceedings in accordance with the laws of this state.

15. Satisfaction, either partial or complete, of the original judgment or of a judgment entered thereupon in any other state shall operate to the same extent as satisfaction of the judgment in this state, except as to costs authorized by subsection 14.

16. The right of a judgment creditor to bring an action to enforce his judgment instead of proceeding under this section remains unimpaired.

17. This section shall be so interpreted and construed as to effectuate its general purpose to make uniform the law of those states which enact it.

18. This section may be cited as the "Uniform Enforcement of Foreign Judgments Law".
revisor_notes: (1974) "Supplemental judgment" purporting to make an original judgment for alimony final which did not give husband notice or opportunity for hearing violated husband's right to due process. Overman v. Overman (A.), 514 S.W.2d 625.

(1974) Held this section not unconstitutional as denying defendant due process of law by depriving him of property prior to hearing on validity of underlying claim. Bittner v. Butts (Mo.), 514 S.W.2d 556.

(1976) In proceedings by judgment creditor, under Illinois summary judgment law, to enforce judgment, held that defendant's allegation that judgment was based on affidavit containing fraudulent misstatements alleged only intrinsic fraud and was not sufficient to authorize equitable relief against enforcement of judgment under Illinois law and therefore full faith and credit clause precluded any such collateral inquiry by a Missouri Court. Young Electric, Inc. v. Susman (A.), 533 S.W.2d 625.

(1976) Held, a foreign judgment may be attacked for lack of jurisdiction over the subject matter, failure to give due notice and fraud in the procurement of jurisdiction. These are the attacks that can be made at the time of application for registration of the foreign judgment. Corning Truck and Radiator Service v. J.W.M., Inc. (A.), 542 S.W.2d 520.

(1976) Held, to vitiate a foreign judgment on grounds of fraud in the procurement it must be shown that the fraud was extrinsic or collateral to the issues tried. Intrinsic fraud is unavailing. Mekelburg v. Whitman (A.), 545 S.W.2d 89.

Le Missouri prévoit des mécanismes de dépôt ou d'enregistrement et de reconnaissance, notamment pour les jugements étrangers et les ordonnances alimentaires, mais selon des régimes distincts et plus ciblés.
correspondences.note_en: The article governs applications for recognition or confirmation of enforceability of foreign enforceable titles. Missouri provides filing or registration and recognition mechanisms, particularly for foreign judgments and support orders, but through separate and more narrowly targeted regimes.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article organise le recours contre une déclaration d’exequatur de titres étrangers et fixe une procédure devant le président du tribunal judiciaire. Les dispositions du Missouri prévoient des contestations ou appels en matière d’ordres étrangers enregistrés, mais dans des domaines et selon des procédures différentes.
correspondences.note_en: The article governs appeals from an exequatur declaration concerning foreign titles and assigns them to the president of the judicial court under a special procedure. The Missouri provisions allow contests or appeals concerning registered foreign orders, but in different subject areas and through different procedures.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1522 permet de renoncer au recours en annulation tout en conservant un appel limité contre l’exequatur, dans un délai d’un mois. Les textes du Missouri prévoient des appels contre certaines décisions d’exécution et en fixent la procédure, mais sans renonciation à l’annulation ni délai et motifs identiques.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1522 permits waiver of annulment while preserving a limited appeal from exequatur within one month. Missouri provisions allow appeals from certain enforcement decisions and regulate appellate filing, but contain no equivalent waiver mechanism and use different deadlines and grounds.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1523 ouvre un appel contre le refus de reconnaissance ou d’exequatur et permet à la cour de connaître du recours en annulation. Le RSMo 511.760 prévoit l’appel d’une décision relative à l’enregistrement d’un jugement étranger, tandis que les autres textes règlent l’appel en général, sans recours spécifique contre une sentence arbitrale.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1523 permits an appeal from refusal of recognition or exequatur and allows the appellate court to hear an annulment action. RSMo 511.760 provides appeals from foreign-judgment registration decisions, while the other provisions regulate appeals generally, without a specific arbitral-award annulment remedy.

Les textes du Missouri organisent l'exécution ou la reconnaissance de certains jugements étrangers, avec des conditions et défenses spécifiques, mais ne couvrent pas globalement les actes étrangers.

Les dispositions du Missouri concernent certaines reconnaissances et exécutions étrangères, surtout en matière alimentaire ou pécuniaire, mais ne reprennent ni le rôle notarial ni l’ensemble des instruments visés.
correspondences.note_en: Article 509-3 assigns notarial authorities responsibility for applications concerning cross-border recognition, enforceability, or certification of instruments and titles. norms.heading: Appeals, stay of proceedings granted, when.

norms.text: If the defendant satisfies the court either that an appeal is pending or that he is entitled and intends to appeal from the foreign country judgment, the court may stay the proceedings until the appeal has been determined or until the expiration of a period of time sufficient to enable the defendant to prosecute the appeal.

correspondences.note_fr: Le jugement déclarant la compétence sans statuer au fond suspend l’instance jusqu’à l’expiration du délai d’appel et, en cas d’appel, jusqu’à la décision. RSMo 511.785 prévoit aussi un sursis de la procédure pendant un appel, mais dans le contexte distinct d’un jugement étranger et de manière discrétionnaire.
correspondences.note_en: A jurisdiction ruling that does not decide the merits suspends the proceeding through the appeal period and, if appealed, until the appellate decision. RSMo 511.785 likewise permits a stay pending appeal, but in the distinct context of a foreign-country judgment and on a discretionary basis.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 110 autorise la suspension de l’instance lorsqu’une partie invoque une décision faisant l’objet d’une tierce opposition, d’un recours en révision ou d’un pourvoi en cassation. Le RSMo 511.785 permet une suspension des procédures pendant un appel concernant un jugement étranger, mais dans un contexte et à des conditions plus limités.
correspondences.note_en: Article 110 permits a stay when a party invokes a decision subject to third-party opposition, revision, or cassation review. RSMo 511.785 allows proceedings to be stayed while an appeal from a foreign-country judgment is pending, but in a narrower context and under different conditions.

correspondences.note_fr: La juridiction française peut poursuivre l’instance ou la suspendre. La Rule 74.14 permet de suspendre l’exécution d’un jugement étranger dans certaines circonstances, notamment en cas d’appel. Le RSMo 511.785 permet de suspendre les procédures lorsqu’un appel d’un jugement étranger est pendant ou envisagé.
correspondences.note_en: The French court may proceed or stay the matter. Rule 74.14 permits a stay of enforcement of a foreign judgment in specified circumstances, including a pending or intended appeal. RSMo 511.785 permits staying proceedings when an appeal from a foreign-country judgment is pending or intended.

correspondences.note_fr: Le tribunal arbitral peut suspendre l’instance pour une durée ou jusqu’à un événement, puis révoquer ou abréger le sursis. Les textes du Missouri prévoient des suspensions ou continuations judiciaires comparables, mais dans des contextes déterminés et sans le même pouvoir général du tribunal arbitral.
correspondences.note_en: An arbitral tribunal may stay proceedings for a specified period or until an event, and may revoke or shorten the stay. The Missouri provisions provide comparable stays or continuances, but only in specified judicial contexts and without the same general arbitral power.

norms.heading: Recognition of judgment in situations not covered by uniform law.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: Sections 511.770 to 511.787 do not prevent the recognition of a foreign country judgment in situations not covered by sections 511.770 to 511.787.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article pose le principe général de l'exécution en France des jugements étrangers et actes étrangers selon les conditions légales. Les textes du Missouri organisent l'exécution ou la reconnaissance de certains jugements étrangers, avec des conditions et défenses spécifiques, mais ne couvrent pas globalement les actes étrangers.
correspondences.note_en: The article states a general principle that foreign judgments and foreign official instruments are enforceable according to statutory conditions. Missouri provisions govern enforcement or recognition of specified foreign judgments, subject to particular conditions and defenses, but do not generally cover foreign instruments.

norms.heading: Writs of error in civil cases abolished — review by appeal.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 512 Appeals and Appellate Procedure

norms.text:
1. Writs of error are abolished in civil cases. Review shall be by appeal, which shall constitute a continuation of the proceeding in the trial court and be deemed to present all issues which heretofore have been presented by writ of error and appeal.

2. This section is not intended to apply to criminal cases.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article autorise le pourvoi en cassation contre une décision de sursis rendue en dernier ressort, limité à la violation de la règle de droit. Les textes du Missouri fournis prévoient un appel civil et encadrent le contrôle par la présentation de l’erreur et son effet matériel.
correspondences.note_en: The article permits cassation review of a stay decision rendered at final instance, limited to violation of law. The supplied Missouri texts provide for civil appeals and condition review on presentation of error and its material effect.

correspondences.note_fr: La nullité du jugement ne peut être demandée que par les voies de recours légales. La Rule 74.06 prévoit des mécanismes de relief, notamment pour un jugement irrégulier ou nul, tandis que le Missouri organise l’appel comme voie de réexamen, sans reprendre exactement la règle française d’exclusivité.
correspondences.note_en: Nullity of a judgment may be sought only through statutory avenues of review. Rule 74.06 provides relief mechanisms, including for irregular or void judgments, while Missouri makes appeal the method of civil review without reproducing the French exclusivity rule exactly.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 527 classe les voies de recours françaises entre voies ordinaires (appel, opposition) et extraordinaires (tierce opposition, révision, cassation). Les textes du Missouri prévoient l’appel, la réouverture ou le réexamen du jugement, les motions post-décisionnelles et le transfert extraordinaire, mais pas cette classification complète ni tous ces recours.
correspondences.note_en: Article 527 classifies French remedies as ordinary (appeal, opposition) and extraordinary (third-party opposition, revision, cassation). The Missouri provisions separately provide for appeal, post-disposition review, relief from judgment, and extraordinary transfer, but do not establish the same complete classification or all of those remedies.

correspondences.note_fr: L'appel vise à faire réformer ou annuler par la cour d'appel le jugement d'une juridiction du premier degré, au moyen de sa critique. Les textes du Missouri prévoient la réformation, l'annulation, la confirmation ou le remplacement du jugement par la juridiction d'appel, ainsi que le contrôle par voie d'appel.
correspondences.note_en: An appeal seeks review and correction or annulment by the appellate court of a first-instance judgment. Missouri provisions provide for affirmance, reversal, modification, a new trial, or entry of the judgment that should have been given, through appellate review.

correspondences.note_fr: L'appel saisit la juridiction d'appel pour rejuger l'affaire en fait et en droit, dans les limites prévues par le CPC. Le Missouri considère l'appel comme la continuation de l'instance et permet la révision de la décision ainsi que son remplacement, mais sous des règles de préservation et de contrôle variables selon le type de procès.
correspondences.note_en: An appeal places the matter before the appellate court for a new decision on law and fact, within prescribed limits. Missouri treats an appeal as a continuation of the trial proceeding and authorizes review and replacement of the judgment, but subject to preservation and case-type limitations.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article ouvre le pourvoi en cassation au ministère public. Les textes du Missouri prévoient une voie d'appel en matière civile et le dépôt d'un acte d'appel par une partie ou son mandataire, sans conférer expressément ce droit au ministère public.
correspondences.note_en: The article grants the public prosecutor access to cassation review. Missouri law provides civil appellate review and permits a party or agent to file a notice of appeal, but does not expressly grant that right to the prosecutor.

norms.heading: Who may appeal.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 512 Appeals and Appellate Procedure

revisor_notes: (1971) Where wife was permitted to amend her motion for change of custody to ask for rights of visitation which she received she was nevertheless an aggrieved party and could appeal since to be an alternative relief it must afford final, full, and complete relief. Eissler v. Eissler (A.), 468 S.W.2d 217.

(1971) Appeal from order, entered in a suit by trustees for construction of testamentary trust, designated as interlocutory and sustaining motion for summary judgment by counterclaimants, who asserted that will provisions creating trust were invalid as violative of rule against perpetuities, and directing delivery of property, accounting and hearing on final distribution, was premature. Proctor v. Jacobs (Mo.), 472 S.W.2d 609.

(1972) After defendant rested his case, the court stated "I'm going to find him guilty and sentence him to six months in the City Workhouse and I'll grant him probation." Defendant immediately filed "motion for a new trial or for outright reversal and acquittal", which was overruled. Defendant then filed his notice of appeal. Appellate court held that attempted sentencing before the filing of and ruling on defendant's motion for new trial was premature and void and there was nothing from which appeal could be taken. State v. Summers (A.), 477 S.W.2d 721.

(1972) An order which quashes a writ of garnishment is a final judgment for purposes of an appeal but an order overruling a petition to quash execution of a garnishment is not appealable for the reason that the order does not constitute a final disposition of the cause nor the merits of the garnishment proceeding. Orf v. Computer Institute, Inc. (A.), 480 S.W.2d 73.
(1976) Commissioner of finance is not a "person aggrieved" by a decision of the state banking board and has no standing to sue. Kostman v. Pine Lawn Bank and Trust Co. (Mo.), 540 S.W.2d 72.

(1977) Held, where motion for new trial on all issues was sustained, moving party cannot then appeal from an order denying his motion for a directed verdict since he is not an aggrieved party. Morris v. Patterson (A.), 549 S.W.2d 613.

(1986) A party whose claim is involuntarily dismissed may remain a "party" to the action within the meaning of the term "party to a suit aggrieved by any judgment of any trial court" for purposes of appeal rights. Aherron v. St. John's Mercy Medical Center, 713 S.W.2d 498 (Mo. banc).

(1986) This section grants a right of appeal from an interlocutory judgment in a partition action only where such judgment determines the quantum of party's interest in the property being partitioned. First National Bank of Carrollton V. Eucalyptus, 721 S.W.2d 165 (Mo.App.).
(1974) Held, a denial of a motion for new trial is not an appealable judgment, an appeal must be taken from the underlying judgment. Cady v. Kansas City Southern Railway Co. (A.), 512 S.W.2d 882.
(1974) Held, an order denying defendant's motion to bring in a third party defendant is not a final judgment and is not appealable. Nadler v. Continental Insurance Co. (A.), 511 S.W.2d 446.

(1977) Requirement that court make a division of marital property in a dissolution action is mandatory and failure to comply results in no final judgment in the action. The fact that a final judgment has not been rendered bars an appeal under the provisions of § 512.020, RSMo. Corder v. Corder (A.), 546 S.W.2d 798.

(1977) Held, entry of a decree making final an earlier interlocutory decree does not violate rule requiring a single final judgment. Bolin v. Farmers Alliance Mutual Insurance Co. (Mo.), 549 S.W.2d 886.
(1977) Failure to rule on a counterclaim results in judgment not disposing of all issues and such a judgment is not appealable. Allis-Chalmers Credit Corp. v. Baker (A.), 559 S.W.2d 763.

(2000) There is an implied right to appeal from circuit court order creating fire protection district that excludes disputed land. Tipton Rural Fire Protection District v. Objectors, 34 S.W.3d 404 (Mo.App.W.D.).
(2003) Qualified domestic relations order comes within special order exception of section but requires denomination as a judgment or decree. Brooks v. Brooks, 98 S.W.3d 530 (Mo.banc).

correspondences.note_fr: L’article concerne le montant déterminant la compétence et le seuil d’ouverture de l’appel. Les textes du Missouri fixent certaines limites de compétence (§ 517.011), prévoient la certification au-delà de ces limites (§ 517.081) et énoncent les règles générales d’appel (§ 512.020; Rule 81.01), sans établir ici un seuil monétaire général d’appel.
correspondences.note_en: The article addresses amount-based jurisdiction and the threshold for appeal. Missouri provisions establish certain jurisdictional limits (§ 517.011), certification when those limits are exceeded (§ 517.081), and general appeal rules (§ 512.020; Rule 81.01), but the supplied texts do not provide a general monetary appeal threshold.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article détermine l'appelabilité du jugement selon le montant des demandes, notamment incidentes, et prévoit une exception pour la demande reconventionnelle en dommages-intérêts. Le Missouri reconnaît l'appel des jugements finaux et autorise une demande reconventionnelle supérieure, mais les textes fournis ne reprennent pas ces seuils ni cette exception.
correspondences.note_en: The article determines appealability by the amount of the claims, including incidental claims, with an exception for a counterclaim for damages. Missouri allows appeals from final judgments and permits counterclaims exceeding the opposing claim, but the supplied provisions do not reproduce the monetary thresholds or exception.

frcp.evidence: mmittee Note – 1974 This rule is substantially the same as Rule 13 of the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure

correspondences.note_fr: L'article rend en principe appelable le jugement statuant sur une demande indéterminée. Les textes du Missouri prévoient l'appel des jugements finaux en général, sans règle particulière pour les demandes indéterminées.
correspondences.note_en: The article generally makes a judgment on an indeterminate claim appealable. Missouri provides generally for appeals from final judgments, but the supplied texts contain no specific rule concerning indeterminate claims.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 83 ouvre un appel immédiat contre les décisions statuant exclusivement sur la compétence, y compris lorsqu’une mesure d’instruction ou provisoire est ordonnée. Le RSMo 512.020 énumère certaines décisions interlocutoires susceptibles d’appel, mais ne prévoit pas spécialement les décisions relatives à la compétence.
correspondences.note_en: Article 83 permits an immediate appeal from a ruling exclusively deciding jurisdiction, including one ordering an evidentiary or provisional measure. RSMo 512.020 lists certain appealable interlocutory orders, but does not specifically address jurisdictional rulings.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 90 permet l’appel global d’un jugement statuant à la fois sur la compétence et le fond, puis impose à la cour soit de statuer au fond, soit de renvoyer l’affaire. Les textes du Missouri prévoient l’appel, les pouvoirs de décision au fond et le renvoi, mais pas ce mécanisme propre à la compétence.
correspondences.note_en: Article 90 permits an appeal of the entire judgment and specifies when the appellate court must decide the merits or remand after reversing on jurisdiction. The Missouri provisions address appealability, appellate disposition, and remand, but do not provide this jurisdiction-specific mechanism.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 91 limite l’appel à la compétence lorsque le jugement statuant aussi sur le fond est rendu en dernier ressort, et organise le renvoi après infirmation. Le Missouri reconnaît le contrôle des questions de compétence et règle l’appel, la décision et le renvoi, sans prévoir cette limitation ni l’irrecevabilité correspondante.
correspondences.note_en: Article 91 restricts the appeal to jurisdiction when the merits judgment is rendered as a final-instance decision and provides for remand after reversal. Missouri addresses jurisdictional review, appealability, disposition, and remand, but not this exclusive jurisdictional appeal or the stated inadmissibility rule.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 104 organise le recours contre les décisions de litispendance ou de connexité comme en matière d’incompétence et règle les recours multiples. Les Rule 81.04, RSMo 512.050 et RSMo 512.020 régissent les appels et certaines décisions appelables, mais ne prévoient ni cette assimilation ni la priorité entre cours saisies.
correspondences.note_en: Article 104 governs appeals from lis pendens or connexity decisions as appeals concerning incompetence, including multiple appeals. Rule 81.04, RSMo 512.050, and RSMo 512.020 govern appeals and appealable orders, but do not provide that specific treatment or priority among multiple appellate courts.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article exclut en principe les recours autonomes contre les décisions relatives aux mesures d’instruction, sauf exceptions légales, et permet leur examen avec le jugement au fond. RSMo 512.020 prévoit que l’absence de recours avant le jugement final ne prive pas du contrôle ultérieur; les autres textes renvoient plus généralement au droit de l’appel et à la révision des décisions interlocutoires.
correspondences.note_en: The article generally bars independent appeals from rulings concerning investigative measures, subject to statutory exceptions, while preserving review with the merits judgment. RSMo 512.020 preserves review of pre-judgment rulings on appeal from the final judgment; the other provisions address appellate rights and revision of interlocutory decisions more generally.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article exclut l’opposition et reporte en principe l’appel ou le pourvoi contre les décisions d’exécution d’une mesure d’instruction au recours contre le jugement au fond; il précise aussi leurs formes. RSMo 512.020 permet généralement le contrôle des décisions interlocutoires avec le jugement final, tandis que la règle 74.01 définit notamment le jugement et l’inscription au rôle.
correspondences.note_en: The article bars opposition and generally defers appeal or cassation of decisions concerning the execution of an evidentiary measure until review of the merits judgment, while specifying their forms. RSMo 512.020 generally permits review of interlocutory rulings with the final judgment, and Rule 74.01 addresses judgments and docket-sheet entry.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article autorise, sous conditions strictes, l’appel immédiat d’une décision ordonnant une expertise et en fixe la procédure. Le RSMo 512.020 régit certains appels interlocutoires et le RSMo 512.050 le dépôt de la déclaration d’appel, mais aucun ne prévoit précisément l’appel de l’ordonnance d’expertise avec autorisation du premier président.
correspondences.note_en: The article permits an immediate appeal from an order for an expert examination under strict conditions and prescribes the procedure. RSMo 512.020 governs specified interlocutory appeals and RSMo 512.050 governs filing a notice of appeal, but neither specifically provides for an appeal from an expert-order authorization by a chief appellate judge.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article 320 autorise un recours immédiat contre le jugement ordonnant ou refusant le serment décisoire, indépendamment du fond. Le Missouri encadre le droit et la procédure d'appel, mais les textes fournis ne visent pas spécifiquement ce type d'ordonnance.
correspondences.note_en: Article 320 permits an immediate appeal from an order granting or refusing a decisory oath, independently of the merits. Missouri governs appellate rights and filing procedure, but the supplied provisions do not specifically identify this type of order as appealable.

correspondences.note_fr: La nullité du jugement ne peut être demandée que par les voies de recours légales. La Rule 74.06 prévoit des mécanismes de relief, notamment pour un jugement irrégulier ou nul, tandis que le Missouri organise l’appel comme voie de réexamen, sans reprendre exactement la règle française d’exclusivité.
correspondences.note_en: Nullity of a judgment may be sought only through statutory avenues of review. Rule 74.06 provides relief mechanisms, including for irregular or void judgments, while Missouri makes appeal the method of civil review without reproducing the French exclusivity rule exactly.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article organise l’appel et l’opposition contre l’ordonnance de référé, avec des exceptions et un délai de quinze jours. Les textes du Missouri régissent le droit d’appel, les décisions susceptibles d’appel et le dépôt de la déclaration d’appel, mais ne reprennent ni l’opposition par défaut ni le même délai.
correspondences.note_en: The article governs appeals and opposition to a référé order, including exceptions and a fifteen-day time limit. The Missouri provisions address the right to appeal, appealable orders, and filing a notice of appeal, but do not provide the same default opposition mechanism or deadline.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article autorise l’ancien représentant légal, lorsqu’il cesse ses fonctions et possède un intérêt personnel, à exercer le recours en son nom et prévoit aussi le recours contre lui. RSMo 512.020 détermine plus généralement quelles parties lésées peuvent interjeter appel, sans régler expressément la cessation des fonctions du représentant.
correspondences.note_en: The article permits a former legal representative who has a personal interest to appeal in his or her own name after the representative role ends, and permits an appeal against that person. RSMo 512.020 generally identifies aggrieved parties entitled to appeal but does not specifically address termination of representative authority.

correspondences.note_fr: L'appel est en principe ouvert contre les jugements de première instance, sauf disposition contraire. Le § 512.020 RSMo reconnaît un droit d'appel civil aux parties lésées, mais seulement pour les catégories d'ordres et jugements qu'il énumère; la Rule 81.01 renvoie au droit applicable.
correspondences.note_en: Appeal is generally available against first-instance judgments unless otherwise provided. RSMo 512.020 grants aggrieved parties a civil appeal, but only for the listed categories of orders and judgments; Rule 81.01 simply makes the right statutory.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article rend immédiatement appelables certains jugements partiels ou incidents mettant fin à l'instance. Le § 512.020 RSMo prévoit certains appels interlocutoires, notamment en matière de partage, ainsi que des appels d'ordonnances spécifiées, mais ne reprend pas l'ensemble des catégories françaises.
correspondences.note_en: The article allows immediate appeals from specified partial and terminating interlocutory judgments. RSMo 512.020 permits certain interlocutory appeals, notably in partition actions, and appeals from specified orders, but does not cover all the French categories.

correspondences.note_fr: Les jugements autres que ceux visés ne sont appelables séparément que dans les cas prévus par la loi. Le § 512.020 RSMo énumère les jugements et ordonnances appelables et prévoit le contrôle ultérieur des décisions non attaquées avant le jugement final; la Rule 81.01 renvoie au droit applicable.
correspondences.note_en: Judgments not covered by the rule cannot be appealed independently unless authorized by law. RSMo 512.020 lists appealable judgments and orders and preserves later review of rulings not appealed before final judgment; Rule 81.01 refers the right of appeal to law.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article reconnaît le droit d’appel à toute partie ayant intérêt, sous réserve de renonciation, et l’étend en matière gracieuse à certains tiers notifiés. Le RSMo 512.020 vise toute partie lésée, mais limite les décisions susceptibles d’appel et ne traite ni de la renonciation ni des tiers en matière gracieuse.
correspondences.note_en: The article grants an appeal to any interested party, subject to waiver, and extends it in non-contentious matters to certain notified third parties. RSMo 512.020 covers any aggrieved party but limits appealable decisions and does not address waiver or notified third parties in non-contentious matters.

correspondences.note_fr: Le jugement rendu sur tierce opposition est soumis aux mêmes voies de recours que la décision initiale. Le Missouri prévoit de manière générale le droit d’appel et les décisions susceptibles d’appel, ainsi que les modalités de dépôt, sans énoncer une règle spécifique de transmission des mêmes recours au jugement sur tierce opposition.
correspondences.note_en: A judgment on third-party opposition is subject to the same remedies as the decision from which it arose. Missouri generally provides appeal rights, appealable judgments, and filing procedures, but does not specifically state that a judgment on third-party opposition carries the same remedies as the original decision.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 607 ouvre le pourvoi contre les jugements mettant fin à l’instance en statuant sur une exception de procédure, une fin de non-recevoir ou un autre incident. Le Missouri permet l’appel d’un jugement final, mais les textes fournis ne prévoient pas expressément la règle française pour les décisions incidentes mettant fin à l’instance.
correspondences.note_en: Article 607 allows cassation review of judgments ending the proceedings by ruling on a procedural exception, inadmissibility defense, or other incident. Missouri permits appeal from a final judgment, but the supplied provisions do not expressly adopt the French rule for incident decisions ending the action.
