Rule 81.04 and RSMo 512.070 address filing, contents, and notice of appeal, but use a ten-day period and different conditions; Rule 81.01 merely states that the right of appeal is provided by law.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article 1381-4 organise le recours contre les décisions relatives au certificat successoral européen : personnes habilitées, délai de quinze jours, requête devant le président du tribunal, audition, notification et mesures de délivrance, rectification, modification ou suspension. Les textes du Missouri régissent plus généralement l'appel civil, ses titulaires, son délai, son contenu et sa notification, sans reprendre cette procédure successorale spéciale ni les pouvoirs du président du tribunal.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1381-4 establishes a special challenge procedure for European Certificate of Succession decisions, including standing, a fifteen-day time limit, petition procedure, hearing, notice, and orders for issuance, correction, modification, or suspension. The Missouri provisions generally govern civil appeals, standing, filing deadlines, contents, and notice, but do not provide this specialized succession procedure or the same judicial powers.

norms.heading: Appeals to stay execution, when — bond.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 512 Appeals and Appellate Procedure

norms.text:
1. Appeals shall stay the execution in the following cases:

(1) When the appellant shall be a personal representative, guardian, or conservator, and the action shall be by or against him as such, or when the appellant shall be a county, city, town, township, school district, or other municipality;

(2) When the appellant, at or prior to the time of filing notice of appeal, presents to the court for its approval a supersedeas bond which shall have such surety or sureties as the court requires. The court may also at or prior to the time of filing notice of appeal, by order of record, fix the amount of the supersedeas bond and allow appellant reasonable time, not exceeding twenty days, from the date of the order to file the same subject to the approval of the court or clerk, and such appeal bond, approved by the court or clerk and filed within the time specified in such order, shall have the effect to stay the execution thereafter. If any execution shall have been taken prior to the filing of the bond as so approved by the court or clerk, the same shall be released.

2. The bond shall be conditioned for the satisfaction of the judgment in full together with costs, interest, and damages for delay, if for any reason the appeal is dismissed or if the judgment is affirmed, and to satisfy in full such modification of the judgment and such costs, interest, and damages as the appellate court may adjudge and award. When the judgment is for the recovery of money not otherwise secured, the amount of the bond shall be fixed at such sum as will cover the whole amount of the judgment remaining unsatisfied, costs on the appeal, interest, and damages for delay, unless the court after notice and hearing and for good cause shown fixes a different amount or orders security other than the bond. When the judgment determines the disposition of the property in controversy as in real actions, replevin, and actions to foreclose mortgages, or when such property is in the custody of the sheriff, or when the proceeds of such property or a bond for its value is in the custody or control of the court, the amount of the supersedeas bond shall be fixed at such sum only as will secure the amount recovered for the use and detention of the property, the costs of the action, costs on appeal, interest, and damages for delay. The bond shall indicate the addresses of the sureties.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article 514 rend de droit exécutoires à titre provisoire les décisions de première instance, sauf disposition contraire de la loi ou du jugement. Les textes du Missouri traitent plutôt de la suspension de l'exécution en cas d'appel, notamment par supersedeas bond, sans poser la même règle générale d'exécution provisoire.
correspondences.note_en: Article 514 makes first-instance decisions provisionally enforceable by default, unless the law or judgment provides otherwise. The Missouri provisions instead govern stays of execution on appeal, especially through a supersedeas bond, and do not establish the same general rule of provisional enforceability.

correspondences.note_fr: Le CPC attribue en principe un effet suspensif au délai et à l’exercice du recours ordinaire. Au Missouri, l’appel ne suspend l’exécution que dans certaines hypothèses ou lorsqu’un supersedeas bond est fourni, selon des conditions détaillées.
correspondences.note_en: The CPC generally makes both the appeal period and the appeal itself suspensive. In Missouri, an appeal stays execution only in specified cases or when a supersedeas bond is provided, subject to detailed conditions.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article ouvre un recours contre l’ordonnance de taxe, dans un délai d’un mois, avec effet suspensif automatique. Les règles et sections du Missouri organisent l’appel contre un jugement ou une ordonnance, mais prévoient un délai différent et, pour le sursis, un régime généralement conditionné à un supersedeas bond.
correspondences.note_en: The article permits an appeal from a taxation order within one month and makes the appeal automatically suspensive. The Missouri rules and statutes govern appeals from judgments or orders, but use a different deadline and generally condition a stay on a supersedeas bond.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article interdit l’exécution provisoire du jugement et prévoit que le délai ainsi que l’exercice du pourvoi en cassation suspendent l’exécution. Les textes du Missouri prévoient un sursis de l’exécution en appel seulement dans certains cas ou moyennant une supersedeas bond, et non automatiquement pour tout recours.
correspondences.note_en: The article prohibits provisional enforcement and provides that the cassation period and a cassation appeal stay enforcement. The Missouri provisions stay execution on appeal only in specified cases or upon posting a supersedeas bond, rather than automatically for every appeal.

correspondences.note_fr: Le CPC subordonne l’exécution provisoire à une ordonnance expresse. Les règles du Missouri prévoient plutôt qu’un appel peut suspendre l’exécution, notamment par supersedeas bond ; les textes fournis ne traitent pas spécifiquement de l’exécution provisoire de cette décision.
correspondences.note_en: The CPC makes provisional enforcement dependent on an express order. The Missouri rules instead provide for stays of execution pending appeal, notably through a supersedeas bond; the supplied texts do not specifically address provisional enforcement of this decision.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article prévoit que la décision d’adoption n’est exécutoire provisoirement que si elle l’ordonne et que le pourvoi en cassation, ainsi que le délai pour l’exercer, suspendent l’exécution. Les règles 81.09 et RSMo 512.080 prévoient une suspension de l’exécution en appel sous certaines conditions, notamment la constitution d’un supersedeas bond, tandis que la règle 81.07 concerne les appels tardifs.
correspondences.note_en: The article provides that an adoption decision is provisionally enforceable only if so ordered, and that both the cassation period and a cassation appeal stay execution. Rules 81.09 and RSMo 512.080 stay execution on appeal only in specified circumstances, chiefly upon a supersedeas bond; Rule 81.07 addresses stays in late appeals.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article prévoit que le délai et l’exercice du recours suspendent l’exécution, sauf exécution provisoire. Au Missouri, l’appel ne suspend l’exécution que dans certains cas ou lorsqu’une sûreté est fournie; les règles détaillent le supersedeas bond et son dépôt.
correspondences.note_en: The article provides that the appeal period and the appeal itself stay enforcement unless provisional enforcement has been ordered. In Missouri, an appeal stays execution only in specified cases or upon provision of security; the cited rules govern the supersedeas bond and its filing.

norms.heading: Supersedeas bond requirements, tobacco settlement litigation.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 512 Appeals and Appellate Procedure

norms.text:
1. In order to secure and protect the moneys to be received as a result of the master settlement agreement, as defined in section 196.1000, in civil litigation as to any claim relating to tobacco products involving a signatory, a successor of a signatory, or an affiliate of a signatory to the master settlement agreement, the amount of the required undertaking or bond or equivalent surety to be furnished during the pendency of an appeal or any discretionary appellate review of any judgment granting legal, equitable, or any other form of relief in order to stay the execution thereon during the entire course of appellate review shall be set in accordance with applicable laws or court rules, except that the total appeal bond or equivalent surety that is required of all appellants collectively shall not exceed fifty million dollars, regardless of the value of the judgment. Nothing in this section or any other provision of law shall be construed to eliminate the discretion of the court, for good cause shown, to set the undertaking or bond on appeal in an amount lower than that otherwise established by law.

2. If the appellee proves by a preponderance of the evidence that a party bringing an appeal or seeking a stay, for whom the undertaking has been limited, is purposefully dissipating or diverting assets outside of the ordinary course of its business for the purpose of avoiding ultimate payment of the judgment, a limitation granted pursuant to subsection 1 of this section may be rescinded and the court may enter such orders as are necessary to prevent dissipation or diversion of the assets. An appellant whose bond has been reduced pursuant to subsection 1 of this section shall:

(1) Provide to the court and appellee the most recent statement of assets and liabilities of the appellant that is filed with any federal, state, or foreign regulatory agency;

(2) Provide to the court and appellee on a quarterly basis any subsequent updated statement of assets and liabilities that is filed with any federal, state, or foreign regulatory agency; and

(3) Agree that it will not dissipate or divert assets outside the ordinary course of its business for the purpose of avoiding ultimate payment of the judgment.

3. The provisions of this section shall apply to all cases pending on or after August 28, 2003.

norms.heading: Bond filed, when.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 512 Appeals and Appellate Procedure

norms.text: If a supersedeas bond is not filed within the time specified, or if the bond filed is found insufficient, and if the action is not yet transferred to the appellate court, a bond may be filed at such time before the action is so transferred to the appellate court, as may be fixed by the trial court. After the action is so transferred, application for leave to file a bond may be made only in the appellate court.

norms.heading: Bond or surety required during pendency of appeal, set how.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 512 Appeals and Appellate Procedure

norms.text:
1. In all cases in which there is a count alleging a tort, the amount of the required undertaking or bond or equivalent surety to be furnished during the pendency of an appeal or any discretionary appellate review of any judgment granting legal, equitable, or any other form of relief in order to stay the execution thereon during the entire course of appellate review shall be set in accordance with applicable laws or court rules; except, that the total appeal bond or equivalent surety that is required of all appellants collectively shall not exceed fifty million dollars, regardless of the value of the judgment. Nothing in this section or any other provision of law shall be construed to eliminate the discretion of the court, for good cause shown, to set the undertaking or bond on appeal in an amount lower than that otherwise established by law.

2. If the respondent proves by a preponderance of the evidence that a party bringing an appeal or seeking a stay, for whom the undertaking has been limited, is purposefully dissipating or diverting assets outside of the ordinary course of its business for the purpose of avoiding ultimate payment of the judgment, the limitation granted under subsection 1 of this section may be rescinded and the court may enter such orders as are necessary to prevent dissipation or diversion of the assets. An appellant whose bond has been reduced under subsection 1 of this section shall:

(1) Provide to the court and respondent the most recent statement of assets and liabilities of the appellant that is filed with any federal, state, or foreign regulatory agency;

(2) Provide to the court and respondent on a quarterly basis any subsequent updated statement of assets and liabilities that is filed with any federal, state, or foreign regulatory agency; and

(3) Agree in writing or in court on the record that it will not dissipate or divert assets outside the ordinary course of its business for the purpose of avoiding ultimate payment of the judgment.

3. The provisions of this section shall apply to all judgments entered on or after August 28, 2005.
revisor_notes: Applicability of statute changes to cases filed after August 28, 2005, 538.305

norms.heading: Supersedeas bond — enforcement.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 512 Appeals and Appellate Procedure

norms.text: By entering into a supersedeas bond, the surety submits himself to the jurisdiction of the trial court and his liability may be enforced on motion for judgment thereon, without the necessity of an independent action. A copy of the motion, and such additional notice of the motion as the court requires shall be served like a summons upon a surety who resides and can be found in the county where the judgment was entered, or who maintains an office and agent in said county where and upon whom such service may be made. If the surety is not a resident who can be found in said county, or if he maintains no office and agent for service there, at the time such motion is filed, by entering into such bond he shall be deemed to have irrevocably appointed the clerk of the trial court his agent upon whom any papers affecting his liability on the bond may be served; and the clerk shall forthwith mail copies of any such papers to such surety to his last known address, by registered mail.

norms.heading: Transcript of record — filing — contents — omissions.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 512 Appeals and Appellate Procedure

norms.text:
1. Within the time prescribed by sections 512.130 and 512.140, the appellant shall cause the transcript on appeal, which may be in typewritten form, to be prepared and filed with the clerk of the proper appellate court; and within five days thereafter a copy of the transcript on appeal shall be filed with the clerk of the trial court, which copy shall remain on file in the office of said clerk.

2. The transcript on appeal shall contain all of the record, proceedings and evidence necessary to the determination of all questions to be presented to the appellate court for decision by either appellant or respondent, except that at the direction of either party the transcript shall include all of the evidence in the case; provided however, that costs for any unnecessary part of the transcript which the appellate court finds has been unreasonably caused to be included in the transcript may be taxed against the party requiring its inclusion. The parties may agree in writing upon an abbreviated or partial transcript of the record, proceedings and evidence, with the evidence either in narrative form or in question and answer form, or upon a statement of the case as provided in section 512.120.

3. If the parties agree that the transcript correctly includes all of the record, proceedings and evidence, it need not be approved by the trial court. If an abbreviated transcript is used, it must be approved by the trial court, which may require any additions considered necessary fully to present the questions raised on appeal. If there is any dispute concerning the correctness of any transcript, or any part thereof, or if the parties fail to agree within a reasonable time as to its correctness, the transcript shall be settled and approved by the trial court. If anything material to either party is omitted from the transcript by error or accident or is inadvertently misstated therein, the parties by stipulation, or the trial court, before the transcript is filed in the appellate court, or the appellate court thereafter, on a proper suggestion or of its own initiative, shall direct that the omission or misstatement shall be corrected and any such correction in the appellate court shall be certified by its clerk to the trial court. The appellate court may, if it seems necessary, order that a supplemental transcript on appeal shall be prepared and filed by either party or by the clerk of the trial court including any additional part of the record, proceedings and evidence, or the clerk may be directed to send up any original documents or exhibits.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 979 exige la remise de copies des décisions attaquée et antérieure, à peine d’irrecevabilité, avec possibilité de régularisation. Les Rules 81.12 et 512.110 exigent un dossier ou transcript contenant les éléments nécessaires au jugement de l’appel, tandis que la Rule 84.08 prévoit une procédure de régularisation avant dismissal.
correspondences.note_en: Article 979 requires copies of the challenged and preceding decisions, subject to inadmissibility and possible cure. Rules 81.12 and 512.110 require an appellate record or transcript containing material necessary for review, while Rule 84.08 provides notice and an opportunity to cure appellate default before dismissal.

correspondences.note_fr: Le greffe de la juridiction ayant rendu la décision transmet le dossier, avec les décisions, actes de notification et conclusions, et envoie ultérieurement les pièces reçues. Les Rules 81.12 et RSMo 512.110 régissent le contenu du dossier d’appel et les dossiers ou transcriptions supplémentaires, mais en font principalement la préparation une charge de l’appelant et ne prescrivent pas cette liste exacte de pièces.
correspondences.note_en: The lower-court clerk transmits the case file with the judgment, proof of notification, earlier decision, and pleadings, including later-received documents. Rules 81.12 and RSMo 512.110 govern the contents and supplementation of the appellate record, but primarily place preparation on the appellant and do not require this exact set of documents.

correspondences.note_fr: Le greffier transmet à la Cour de cassation le dossier comprenant notamment la déclaration et la décision attaquée, ainsi que les pièces reçues ultérieurement. Les règles 81.12 et 512.110 organisent le contenu et la transmission du dossier d'appel, mais confient principalement sa préparation à l'appelant et ne reprennent pas exactement cette obligation du greffier.
correspondences.note_en: The clerk transmits the case file, including the appeal declaration and challenged decision, and later-received documents, to the Court of Cassation. Rules 81.12 and 512.110 govern the contents and transmission of an appellate record, but primarily place preparation duties on the appellant and do not reproduce the same clerk-transmission obligation.

norms.heading: Agreed statement of case.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 512 Appeals and Appellate Procedure

norms.text: When the questions presented by an appeal can be determined without an examination of all the pleadings, evidence, and proceedings in the court below, the parties may prepare and sign a statement of the case showing how the questions arose and were decided in the trial court and setting forth only so many of the facts averred and proved or sought to be proved as are essential to a decision of the questions by the appellate court. The statement shall include a copy of the judgment or order appealed from, a copy of the notice of appeal with its filing date, and a concise statement of the points to be relied on by the appellant. If the statement conforms to the truth, it, together with such additions as the court may consider necessary fully to present the questions raised by the appeal, shall be approved by the trial court and shall then be certified to the appellate court as the transcript on appeal.

norms.heading: Transcript, when filed.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 512 Appeals and Appellate Procedure

norms.text: The transcript on appeal shall be filed with, and the action transferred to, the appellate court within ninety days from the date of filing of the notice of appeal, except that, when more than one appeal is taken from the same judgment or order to the same appellate court, the trial court may prescribe the time for filing and transferring, which in no event shall be less than ninety days from the date of filing of the first notice of appeal.

norms.heading: Extension of time by trial court.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 512 Appeals and Appellate Procedure

norms.text: The trial court may extend the time within which any act may be done under sections 512.110 and 512.130, in accordance with subsection 2 of section 506.060.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 645 rend générales les prorogations de délais prévues par les articles 643 et 644, sous réserve des dérogations expresses, notamment en matière d’élections. La Rule 44.01(b), RSMo 512.140 et la Rule 81.20 permettent certaines extensions, mais dans des domaines et sous des conditions différentes, sans règle générale équivalente.
correspondences.note_en: Article 645 makes the extensions under Articles 643 and 644 generally applicable, subject to express exceptions, especially for election appeals. Rule 44.01(b), RSMo 512.140, and Rule 81.20 authorize extensions in specified contexts, but do not provide the same general rule or election-specific limitation.

norms.heading: Rules for filing briefs, transcripts, and docketing cases.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 512 Appeals and Appellate Procedure

norms.text:
1. All briefs shall be prepared as provided by rule of the appellate court. The appellate courts shall have power to prescribe the number of copies which shall be filed; the time within which briefs shall be filed and the manner in which transcripts on appeal, briefs, and other documents shall be served upon the opposite party or otherwise made available to him; the time and manner in which appeals shall be docketed and set for argument; and rules for the taxation of the costs of preparing transcripts on appeal. Any appellate court may suspend or modify the rules made in pursuance of this section in a particular case upon a showing that justice requires a suspension or modification, and shall do so especially when a litigant is a poor person and the general rules require a burdensome expenditure of money.

2. Any rules made by an appellate court under subsection 1 with relation to the docketing of cases and setting the same for argument shall prevail over any statutory provision prescribing the order of hearings or preferences to be given in certain classes of cases.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article 924 permet à l'intimé constitué de demander la fixation d'une audience dans les deux mois de l'appel. La Rule 84.02 prévoit une conférence de mise au rôle et la fixation de l'affaire pour argumentation, et RSMo 512.150 habilite les juridictions d'appel à fixer les délais et l'ordre des audiences, sans reprendre ce délai ni cette initiative de l'intimé.
correspondences.note_en: Article 924 allows an appearing respondent to request that a hearing be set within two months after the appeal. Rule 84.02 provides appellate docketing and setting for argument, and RSMo 512.150 authorizes rules on docketing and hearing dates, but neither adopts the same deadline or respondent-initiated mechanism.

correspondences.note_fr: Le premier président fixe la date et l’heure d’appel de l’affaire, peut désigner la chambre de distribution et en avise les avocats constitués. La Rule 84.02 prévoit la mise au rôle et la fixation de l’affaire pour argumentation, tandis que le RSMo 512.150 habilite les cours à régler ces modalités, sans reprendre la désignation de chambre ni l’avis prévu.
correspondences.note_en: The first president sets the date and time for calling the case, may designate the assigned chamber, and notifies counsel. Rule 84.02 addresses docketing and setting appellate cases for argument, while RSMo 512.150 authorizes rules on those matters, but neither covers chamber designation and notice in the same terms.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1009 permet de réduire les délais de dépôt des mémoires et pièces, après avis du procureur général, et impose alors la fixation de l’audience. Les règles 84.05 et RSMo 512.150 permettent de modifier les délais de dépôt, mais ne reprennent pas l’ensemble de ce mécanisme. Les règles 100.02 et 81.20 concernent principalement le dossier, non les mémoires et pièces.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1009 allows filing deadlines for briefs and documents to be shortened after consulting the public prosecutor, and then requires the hearing date to be set. Rules 84.05 and RSMo 512.150 permit filing deadlines to be modified, but do not reproduce the full mechanism. Rules 100.02 and 81.20 principally concern the record, not briefs and documents.

norms.heading: Questions considered on appeal — disposition by court — damages — executions.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 512 Appeals and Appellate Procedure

norms.text:
1. Apart from questions of jurisdiction of the trial court over the subject matter and questions as to the sufficiency of pleadings to state a claim upon which relief can be granted or a legal defense to a claim, no allegations of error shall be considered in any civil appeal except such as have been presented to or expressly decided by the trial court.

2. No appellate court shall reverse any judgment, unless it believes that error was committed by the trial court against the appellant, and materially affecting the merits of the action.

3. The appellate court shall examine the transcript on appeal and, subject to the provision of subsections 1 and 2, award a new trial or partial new trial, reverse or affirm the judgment or order of the trial court, or give such judgment as such court ought to have given, as to the appellate court shall seem agreeable to law. Unless justice requires otherwise the court shall dispose finally of the case on appeal and no new trial shall be ordered as to issues in which no error appears.

4. Upon the affirmance of any judgment or order, or upon the dismissal of any case, the appellate court may award to the respondent such damages not exceeding ten percent of the amount of the judgment complained of as may be just, and when such judgment shall be affirmed for part of the sum of which judgment was rendered by the trial court, such part of said judgment shall bear lawful interest from the date of the rendition of the original judgment in the trial court.

5. The appellate court, upon the determination of any case on appeal, may award execution to carry the same into effect, or may remand the case, with the decision, to the trial court from whence the cause came, and such determination shall be carried into execution by such trial court.
revisor_notes: (1986) An appeal which amounts to nothing more than a request that the court of appeals substitute its judgment for that of a trial court is held frivolous. An assertion on an appeal of a position diametrically opposite of one taken at trial is held frivolous. Swanigan v. Crochett, 713 S.W.2d 41 (Mo.App.).

correspondences.note_fr: L'article 76 encadre le relevé d'office de l'incompétence d'attribution, avec des conditions particulières et des restrictions en appel. Rule 55.27(g)(3) impose au tribunal de rejeter l'action dès que l'absence de subject-matter jurisdiction apparaît, tandis que RSMo 512.160 préserve cette question en appel, selon un régime différent et plus large.
correspondences.note_en: Article 76 restricts sua sponte subject-matter jurisdiction rulings and adds special appellate limits. Rule 55.27(g)(3) requires dismissal whenever lack of subject-matter jurisdiction appears, while RSMo 512.160 preserves that issue on appeal, but under a different and broader regime.

correspondences.note_fr: La cour renvoie l'affaire à la juridiction qu'elle estime compétente, et ce renvoi s'impose aux parties et au juge de renvoi. Les règles du Missouri prévoient le renvoi par la juridiction d'appel au tribunal inférieur avec la décision, mais dans le cadre général de l'appel plutôt que pour incompétence.
correspondences.note_en: The French article requires remand to the court deemed competent and makes the decision binding on the parties and the remitting court. Missouri provisions allow an appellate court to remand a case with its decision for execution, but as a general appellate mechanism rather than specifically for jurisdictional incompetence.

correspondences.note_fr: Lorsque la cour d'appel est aussi la juridiction d'appel du tribunal compétent, elle peut statuer au fond pour donner une solution définitive, après instruction si nécessaire. Les textes du Missouri permettent également à la cour d'appel de rendre le jugement qui aurait dû être rendu et de régler définitivement l'affaire, mais sans la condition particulière liée au renvoi pour incompétence.
correspondences.note_en: When the appellate court also has appellate jurisdiction over the court deemed competent, it may decide the merits and finally dispose of the case, after any necessary inquiry. Missouri provisions likewise authorize the appellate court to enter the judgment that should have been entered and finally dispose of the case, but without the French jurisdictional-remand condition.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 90 permet l’appel global d’un jugement statuant à la fois sur la compétence et le fond, puis impose à la cour soit de statuer au fond, soit de renvoyer l’affaire. Les textes du Missouri prévoient l’appel, les pouvoirs de décision au fond et le renvoi, mais pas ce mécanisme propre à la compétence.
correspondences.note_en: Article 90 permits an appeal of the entire judgment and specifies when the appellate court must decide the merits or remand after reversing on jurisdiction. The Missouri provisions address appealability, appellate disposition, and remand, but do not provide this jurisdiction-specific mechanism.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 91 limite l’appel à la compétence lorsque le jugement statuant aussi sur le fond est rendu en dernier ressort, et organise le renvoi après infirmation. Le Missouri reconnaît le contrôle des questions de compétence et règle l’appel, la décision et le renvoi, sans prévoir cette limitation ni l’irrecevabilité correspondante.
correspondences.note_en: Article 91 restricts the appeal to jurisdiction when the merits judgment is rendered as a final-instance decision and provides for remand after reversal. Missouri addresses jurisdictional review, appealability, disposition, and remand, but not this exclusive jurisdictional appeal or the stated inadmissibility rule.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article autorise le pourvoi en cassation contre une décision de sursis rendue en dernier ressort, limité à la violation de la règle de droit. Les textes du Missouri fournis prévoient un appel civil et encadrent le contrôle par la présentation de l’erreur et son effet matériel.
correspondences.note_en: The article permits cassation review of a stay decision rendered at final instance, limited to violation of law. The supplied Missouri texts provide for civil appeals and condition review on presentation of error and its material effect.

correspondences.note_fr: L'appel vise à faire réformer ou annuler par la cour d'appel le jugement d'une juridiction du premier degré, au moyen de sa critique. Les textes du Missouri prévoient la réformation, l'annulation, la confirmation ou le remplacement du jugement par la juridiction d'appel, ainsi que le contrôle par voie d'appel.
correspondences.note_en: An appeal seeks review and correction or annulment by the appellate court of a first-instance judgment. Missouri provisions provide for affirmance, reversal, modification, a new trial, or entry of the judgment that should have been given, through appellate review.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 559 sanctionne l’appel principal dilatoire ou abusif par une amende civile pouvant être assortie de dommages-intérêts. La Rule 84.19 permet d’accorder des dommages-intérêts en cas d’appel frivole, tandis que le RSMo 512.160(4) prévoit des dommages-intérêts après confirmation ou rejet, sans amende civile spécifique.
correspondences.note_en: Article 559 sanctions a dilatory or abusive principal appeal with a civil fine and potentially damages. Rule 84.19 permits damages for a frivolous appeal, while RSMo 512.160(4) permits damages after affirmance or dismissal, but neither provides the same civil-fine mechanism.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 560 permet d’accorder des dommages-intérêts contre celui qui interjette appel après s’être abstenu sans motif légitime de comparaître en première instance. La Rule 84.19 vise les appels frivoles et le RSMo 512.160(4) les dommages-intérêts après confirmation ou rejet, sans reprendre la condition de non-comparution.
correspondences.note_en: Article 560 authorizes damages against an appellant who unjustifiably failed to appear at trial. Rule 84.19 addresses frivolous appeals, and RSMo 512.160(4) allows damages after affirmance or dismissal, but neither incorporates the article’s specific failure-to-appear condition.

correspondences.note_fr: L'appel saisit la juridiction d'appel pour rejuger l'affaire en fait et en droit, dans les limites prévues par le CPC. Le Missouri considère l'appel comme la continuation de l'instance et permet la révision de la décision ainsi que son remplacement, mais sous des règles de préservation et de contrôle variables selon le type de procès.
correspondences.note_en: An appeal places the matter before the appellate court for a new decision on law and fact, within prescribed limits. Missouri treats an appeal as a continuation of the trial proceeding and authorizes review and replacement of the judgment, but subject to preservation and case-type limitations.

correspondences.note_fr: La dévolution est limitée aux chefs du dispositif critiqués et à ceux qui en dépendent, sauf appel-annulation. Le Missouri exige que l'avis désigne le jugement attaqué et que les points d'appel identifient les erreurs, mais les textes fournis ne prévoient pas expressément la règle française des chefs dépendants ni la dévolution intégrale en cas d'annulation.
correspondences.note_en: Appellate jurisdiction is limited to expressly challenged dispositions and dependent dispositions, except when annulment is sought. Missouri requires designation of the judgment and specification of appellate errors, but the supplied provisions do not expressly provide the French dependent-issues rule or automatic total devolution upon annulment.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 568 permet à la cour d’appel, après infirmation ou annulation dans certains cas, d’évoquer les points non jugés et de statuer définitivement, éventuellement après une mesure d’instruction. Les textes du Missouri autorisent une disposition finale et le jugement que la cour estime devoir rendre, mais ne prévoient pas expressément cette évocation dans les mêmes conditions.
correspondences.note_en: Article 568 permits the court of appeal, after reversal or annulment in specified circumstances, to take over undecided issues and decide the case finally, potentially after conducting its own evidentiary measure. Missouri provisions authorize final disposition and the judgment the appellate court ought to give, but do not expressly provide for evocation under the same conditions.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 570 répartit la compétence pour l’exécution de l’arrêt d’appel entre la juridiction de première instance et la juridiction d’appel, avec possibilité de retenir ou de désigner l’exécution. Le RSMo 512.160(5) permet à la juridiction d’appel d’ordonner l’exécution ou de renvoyer l’affaire au tribunal de première instance, sans reprendre toute cette répartition.
correspondences.note_en: Article 570 allocates authority to enforce an appellate judgment between the first-instance and appellate courts, allowing the appellate court to retain or designate enforcement. RSMo 512.160(5) allows the appellate court to award execution or remand the case to the trial court, but does not reproduce the full allocation scheme.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 581 sanctionne le recours dilatoire ou abusif par une amende civile pouvant atteindre 10 000 euros, sans préjudice de dommages-intérêts. La Rule 84.19 permet des dommages pour appel frivole, et le RSMo 512.160 autorise certains dommages en cas de confirmation ou de rejet, mais aucun ne reprend exactement l’amende et le régime de l’article 581.
correspondences.note_en: Article 581 authorizes a civil fine of up to €10,000 for a dilatory or abusive remedy, without prejudice to damages. Rule 84.19 permits damages for a frivolous appeal, and RSMo 512.160 allows certain damages after affirmance or dismissal, but neither reproduces the article’s exact fine and framework.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 602 limite la révision au seul chef du jugement concerné, sauf dépendance entre les chefs. La Rule 74.01(b) permet la révision d’une décision concernant seulement certaines demandes avant le jugement final, tandis que les Rules 78.01 et RSMo 512.160 prévoient respectivement un nouveau procès ou un nouveau procès partiel.
correspondences.note_en: Article 602 limits revision to the affected part of the judgment unless the other parts depend on it. Rule 74.01(b) allows revision of an order resolving fewer claims before final judgment, while Rules 78.01 and RSMo 512.160 address new trials or partial new trials.

correspondences.note_fr: Le pourvoi vise à faire censurer la non-conformité d’un jugement aux règles de droit. Le § 512.160 et la Rule 84.13 autorisent une juridiction d’appel à réformer un jugement en cas d’erreur du tribunal de première instance affectant matériellement le fond de l’affaire. La Rule 83.04 organise un transfert extraordinaire après l’arrêt de la cour d’appel.
correspondences.note_en: A cassation appeal seeks to have a judgment censured for nonconformity with rules of law. Section 512.160 and Rule 84.13 allow an appellate court to reverse a judgment for trial-court error materially affecting the merits. Rule 83.04 provides extraordinary transfer after a court of appeals opinion.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 619 interdit en principe les moyens nouveaux devant la Cour de cassation, avec des exceptions pour les moyens de pur droit et ceux nés de la décision attaquée. Le Missouri impose aussi la préservation et la présentation des erreurs, mais selon des exceptions et une structure d’appel différentes.
correspondences.note_en: Article 619 generally bars new grounds before the Court of Cassation, subject to exceptions for pure questions of law and grounds arising from the challenged decision. Missouri likewise requires appellate preservation and briefing, but uses different exceptions and an appellate, rather than cassation, framework.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article permet une cassation totale ou partielle selon la dissociabilité des chefs. Rule 84.14 et RSMo 512.160(3) permettent fonctionnellement d’infirmer ou d’ordonner un nouveau procès pour tout ou partie du jugement, mais dans le cadre de l’appel.
correspondences.note_en: The article permits total or partial cassation depending on whether the claims are severable. Rule 84.14 and RSMo 512.160(3) functionally allow reversal or a new trial as to all or part of a judgment, but in an appeal proceeding.

correspondences.note_fr: La cassation rétablit les parties dans leur situation antérieure et annule de plein droit les décisions qui en dépendent ; elle peut aussi mettre certaines parties hors de cause. Le Missouri prévoit la réformation, le règlement définitif, le renvoi et l’exécution de la décision d’appel, sans organiser expressément ces effets consécutifs.
correspondences.note_en: Cassation restores the parties to their pre-judgment position, automatically nullifies dependent decisions, and may remove parties from the remand proceedings. Missouri provides reversal, final disposition, remand, and execution of the appellate decision, but does not expressly provide these consequential effects.

correspondences.note_fr: En cas de cassation avec renvoi, la Cour désigne la juridiction de renvoi, qui statue conformément aux règles applicables. Les textes du Missouri permettent à la juridiction d’appel de renvoyer l’affaire avec sa décision au tribunal d’origine, mais ne prévoient pas ici le mécanisme français de désignation.
correspondences.note_en: After a reversal with remand, the French court designates the remand court, which then decides under the applicable rules. Missouri allows the appellate court to remand the case with its decision to the originating trial court, but does not provide the French designation mechanism here.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 628 sanctionne le pourvoi abusif par une amende civile et une indemnité au profit du défendeur. La Rule 84.19 permet d’accorder des dommages-intérêts en cas d’appel frivole, tandis que le RSMo 512.160 autorise certains dommages en cas de confirmation ou de rejet, mais aucun des deux ne reprend exactement le régime de l’amende civile.
correspondences.note_en: Article 628 sanctions an abusive cassation appeal with a civil fine and an award to the respondent. Rule 84.19 permits damages for a frivolous appeal, and RSMo 512.160 permits certain damages after affirmance or dismissal, but neither reproduces the civil-fine scheme exactly.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 631 prévoit qu’après cassation, l’instruction reprend devant la juridiction de renvoi dans l’état de la procédure non atteint par la cassation. Le § 512.160(5) et la Rule 84.28 prévoient le renvoi et l’exécution de la décision d’appel, sans reprendre expressément cette règle sur l’état de la procédure.
correspondences.note_en: Article 631 provides that, after cassation, proceedings before the remand court resume in the procedural state unaffected by the cassation. RSMo 512.160(5) and Rule 84.28 provide for remand and enforcement of the appellate disposition, but do not expressly address resuming the unaffected procedural record.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 634 maintient, après cassation, les moyens et prétentions antérieurement soumis lorsque les parties n’en présentent pas de nouveaux, y compris en cas de défaut de comparution. RSMo 512.160 impose une limitation comparable des erreurs pouvant être invoquées en appel, mais ne règle pas la reprise d’instance après cassation.
correspondences.note_en: Article 634 preserves the arguments and claims previously submitted after cassation when parties present no new ones, including nonappearing parties. RSMo 512.160 comparably limits appellate issues to matters presented to or decided by the trial court, but does not govern post-cassation proceedings.

correspondences.note_fr: L’affaire est rejugée en fait et en droit par la juridiction de renvoi, sauf les chefs non cassés. Le Missouri prévoit qu’une affaire renvoyée peut être entendue à nouveau et exécutée par le tribunal saisi, mais ne reprend pas expressément la limitation aux chefs atteints par la cassation.
correspondences.note_en: The case is reheard on fact and law by the remand court, except for issues unaffected by the reversal. Missouri provides for a case to be heard anew and for the remand court to implement the appellate disposition, but does not expressly state the limitation to reversed issues.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article fixe les chefs critiqués par les premières conclusions et impose la présentation initiale de l’ensemble des prétentions au fond, sous réserve de certaines réponses ou demandes nouvelles. La Rule 84.04 structure les points et le relief demandé, tandis que les Rules 84.13 et le RSMo 512.160 limitent l’examen aux erreurs présentées et préservées.
correspondences.note_en: The article fixes the challenged judgment provisions through the first submissions and generally requires all merits claims to be presented initially, subject to specified later claims. Rule 84.04 structures appellate issues and relief, while Rule 84.13 and RSMo 512.160 limit review to properly presented and preserved matters.

correspondences.note_fr: Lorsque l’affaire est renvoyée devant une juridiction du fond, les règles du renvoi après cassation s’appliquent. Rule 84.28 et RSMo 512.160(5) permettent le renvoi de la cause au tribunal inférieur avec la décision de la juridiction d’appel, sans reprendre l’ensemble des règles de procédure du renvoi.
correspondences.note_en: When the case is remanded to a trial court, the procedures applicable after cassation govern. Rule 84.28 and RSMo 512.160(5) authorize remand with the appellate decision, but do not set out the full procedure applicable to the remand.

correspondences.note_fr: La cour d'appel peut remplacer la décision attaquée par celle qu'elle estime devoir rendre, tandis que les autorités de première instance restent temporairement compétentes et doivent transmettre leurs décisions. Les Rules 84.14 et 512.160(3) couvrent le pouvoir de statuer à nouveau; la Rule 84.28 couvre le renvoi, mais pas le régime particulier de compétence et de transmission.
correspondences.note_en: The appellate court may substitute the judgment it considers proper, while the first-instance authorities retain limited competence and must transmit intervening decisions. Rules 84.14 and 512.160(3) cover appellate disposition, and Rule 84.28 covers remand, but none addresses the specific continuing jurisdiction and transmission mechanism.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1247 permet, en cas de rejet de l’appel, de condamner l’appelant — sauf le juge — aux dépens et à des dommages-intérêts. Les règles du Missouri prévoient séparément la charge des frais d’appel et l’octroi éventuel de dommages pour appel frivole, affirmation ou rejet, avec des conditions et effets différents.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1247 permits the rejected appellant—except the judge—to be ordered to pay costs and damages. Missouri separately addresses appellate costs and possible damages for frivolous appeals, affirmance, or dismissal, but under materially different conditions and effects.

correspondences.note_fr: L’appel peut réformer ou annuler la sentence, la cour statuant en droit ou en amiable composition dans les limites de la mission arbitrale. Les textes du Missouri organisent plutôt les pouvoirs ordinaires de la cour d’appel — confirmer, infirmer, ordonner un nouveau procès ou rendre le jugement approprié — sans prévoir l’amiable composition ni la limite propre à la mission arbitrale.
correspondences.note_en: An appeal may reform or annul the award, with the court deciding in law or as amiable compositeur within the tribunal’s mandate. Missouri appellate provisions instead address ordinary powers to affirm, reverse, order a new trial, or enter the proper judgment, without the arbitration-specific amiable-composition and mandate limitations.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1498 règle l’exequatur d’une sentence arbitrale pendant ou après le recours, notamment lorsque l’appel ou le recours en annulation est rejeté. Le RSMo 512.160(5) permet à la juridiction d’appel d’ordonner l’exécution après la décision, mais ne prévoit ni l’exequatur ni le régime propre aux sentences arbitrales.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1498 governs exequatur of an arbitral award during or after review, including when an appeal or annulment action is rejected. RSMo 512.160(5) allows an appellate court to award execution after deciding an appeal, but does not provide for exequatur or the special treatment of arbitral awards.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article 1500 permet l'appel de l'ordonnance refusant l'exequatur dans le mois et permet à la cour de connaître simultanément du recours contre la sentence lorsque le délai est encore ouvert. Les textes du Missouri organisent l'appel des jugements et ordres, son délai et le pouvoir de la cour, sans règle spécifique sur l'exequatur ou la jonction avec le recours contre la sentence.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1500 permits an appeal from refusal of exequatur within one month and allows the appellate court to hear the award challenge if still timely. Missouri governs appeals from judgments and orders, their filing deadline, and appellate disposition, but has no specific exequatur or linked-award-review rule.

norms.heading: Practice of supreme court to apply to court of appeals.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 512 Appeals and Appellate Procedure

norms.text: The provisions of the civil code, concerning practice in civil cases, regulating the practice in the supreme court and the manner of taking appeals, shall apply to practice in the court of appeals, so far as the same may be applicable.

norms.heading: Appeals from cases tried before associate circuit judge.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 512 Appeals and Appellate Procedure

norms.text:
1. Any person aggrieved by a judgment in a civil case tried without a jury before an associate circuit judge, other than an associate circuit judge sitting in the probate division or who has been assigned to hear the case on the record under procedures applicable before circuit judges, shall have the right of a trial de novo in all cases tried before municipal court or under the provisions of chapter 482 or 535.

2. In all other contested civil cases tried with or without a jury before an associate circuit judge or on assignment under such procedures applicable before circuit judges or in any misdemeanor case or county ordinance violation case a record shall be kept, and any person aggrieved by a judgment rendered in any such case may have an appeal upon that record to the appropriate appellate court. At the discretion of the judge, but in compliance with the rules of the Supreme Court, the record may be a stenographic record or one made by the utilization of electronic, magnetic, or mechanical sound or video recording devices.

norms.heading: Perfecting right of trial de novo, how.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 512 Appeals and Appellate Procedure

norms.text:
1. The right of trial de novo provided in subsection 1 of section 512.180 shall be perfected by filing an application for trial de novo with the clerk serving the associate circuit judge within ten days after the judgment is rendered. A copy of the application shall be mailed by the clerk to the opposing party or his attorney of record or served upon him as provided by law for the service of notices within fifteen days after the judgment was rendered. No application for a trial de novo shall stay execution unless and until the applicant, or some person for him, together with one or more solvent sureties to be approved by the associate circuit judge, within the time prescribed in the first sentence of this section, enter into a recognizance before the associate circuit judge to the adverse party, in a sum sufficient to secure the payment of such judgment and costs, conditioned that the applicant will prosecute his application for trial de novo with due diligence to a decision, and that if on such trial de novo judgment be given against him, he will pay such judgment, and that, if his application for trial de novo be dismissed, he will pay the judgment rendered by the associate circuit judge, together with the costs.

2. Appeals to the court of appeals or to the supreme court shall be governed by the same rules applicable to appeals from judgments rendered by circuit judges.

norms.heading: Form of recognizance.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 512 Appeals and Appellate Procedure

norms.text:
Such recognizance must be signed by the parties entering into the same, and be approved by the associate circuit judge, and may be in the following form:

We the undersigned, ______ and ______, acknowledge ourselves indebted to ______ in the sum of ______ dollars, to be void upon this condition. Whereas, ______ has made application for a trial de novo from a judgment of ______, an associate circuit judge, in an action between ______, plaintiff, and ______, defendant; now, if on such trial de novo judgment be given against the applicant, and he shall satisfy such judgment, or if his application shall be dismissed, and he shall pay the judgment of the associate circuit judge, together with the cost of the appeal, this recognizance shall be void.

______

A B

______

C D

Approved ______, day of ______, 20______

__________________

Associate Circuit Judge

norms.heading: Application for trial de novo — release of property taken under execution.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 512 Appeals and Appellate Procedure

norms.text: If an application for trial de novo is timely filed and a bond be given and approved and, in the meantime, execution shall have been issued, the associate circuit judge shall give the applicant a certificate that an application for trial de novo in the cause has been allowed and bond given, and on presentation of such certificate to the sheriff, he shall forthwith release the property of the defendant that may have been taken in execution.

norms.heading: Associate circuit judge or clerk to file transcript with clerk for trial de novo.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 512 Appeals and Appellate Procedure

norms.text: When an application for a trial de novo is timely filed, the associate circuit judge or the clerk who has custody of the case papers shall forthwith transmit the case papers in the cause or a transcript thereof to the clerk receiving cases originally filed for hearing and determination before a circuit judge, and the cause shall thereupon be assigned for a trial de novo before a circuit or associate circuit judge in accordance with assignment procedures prescribed by local circuit court rule or as directed by the presiding judge of the circuit.

norms.heading: Judge assigned to hear case anew.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 512 Appeals and Appellate Procedure

norms.text: The judge assigned to hear the cause shall proceed to hear, try and determine the same anew with a record of the proceedings being made, without regarding any error, defect or other imperfection on the trial, judgment or other proceedings of the associate circuit judge in relation to the cause.

correspondences.note_fr: L’affaire est rejugée en fait et en droit par la juridiction de renvoi, sauf les chefs non cassés. Le Missouri prévoit qu’une affaire renvoyée peut être entendue à nouveau et exécutée par le tribunal saisi, mais ne reprend pas expressément la limitation aux chefs atteints par la cassation.
correspondences.note_en: The case is reheard on fact and law by the remand court, except for issues unaffected by the reversal. Missouri provides for a case to be heard anew and for the remand court to implement the appellate disposition, but does not expressly state the limitation to reversed issues.

norms.heading: Same cause to be heard — necessary parties may be added.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 512 Appeals and Appellate Procedure

norms.text: The same cause of action, and no other, that was tried before the associate circuit judge, shall be tried before the judge upon the trial de novo; provided, that new parties, plaintiff or defendant, necessary to a complete determination of the cause of action, may be added in the trial de novo.
revisor_notes: (1976) Held that supreme court rule overrides this section and that third party practice, (court rule 41.01(b) controls. State ex rel. Mayweather v. Bondurant (A.), 538 S.W.2d 953.

(1985) Plaintiff's amendment to increase the amount of damages in the trial de novo was proper where the same cause of action based on the same theory and supported by the same ultimate facts was heard in the trial de novo. McMenamy v. Main (Mo.App.), 686 S.W.2d 874.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 633 renvoie, pour la recevabilité des prétentions nouvelles, aux règles applicables devant la juridiction dont la décision a été cassée. Les §§ 512.280, 512.290 et 512.300 encadrent pareillement les prétentions, demandes reconventionnelles et modifications nouvelles lors d’un trial de novo, mais dans ce cadre particulier.
correspondences.note_en: Article 633 subjects new claims to the rules applicable before the court whose decision was quashed. RSMo 512.280, 512.290, and 512.300 similarly regulate new claims, counterclaims, and amendments in a trial de novo, but only within that specific proceeding.

norms.heading: No setoff or counterclaim to be pleaded in trial de novo, when.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 512 Appeals and Appellate Procedure

norms.text: In cases wherein the summons shall be personally served on the defendant, no setoff nor counterclaim shall be pleaded in the trial de novo proceedings that was not pleaded before the associate circuit judge.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 564 interdit en appel les prétentions nouvelles, sous réserve d’exceptions précises. Le RSMo 512.290 interdit seulement, dans certains procès de novo, les demandes en compensation ou reconventionnelles non présentées devant le juge initial ; il est donc plus étroit.
correspondences.note_en: Article 564 bars new claims on appeal, subject to specified exceptions. RSMo 512.290 bars only setoffs or counterclaims not previously pleaded in certain trials de novo, so it is substantially narrower.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 567 rend recevables en appel les demandes reconventionnelles. La section 512.290 traite directement des demandes reconventionnelles lors d’un trial de novo, mais interdit celles qui n’ont pas été présentées devant le juge de proximité; la règle est donc matériellement différente et plus restrictive.
correspondences.note_en: Article 567 makes counterclaims admissible on appeal. RSMo 512.290 directly addresses counterclaims in a trial de novo, but bars counterclaims not pleaded before the associate circuit judge; it is therefore materially narrower and only partially equivalent.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 633 renvoie, pour la recevabilité des prétentions nouvelles, aux règles applicables devant la juridiction dont la décision a été cassée. Les §§ 512.280, 512.290 et 512.300 encadrent pareillement les prétentions, demandes reconventionnelles et modifications nouvelles lors d’un trial de novo, mais dans ce cadre particulier.
correspondences.note_en: Article 633 subjects new claims to the rules applicable before the court whose decision was quashed. RSMo 512.280, 512.290, and 512.300 similarly regulate new claims, counterclaims, and amendments in a trial de novo, but only within that specific proceeding.

norms.heading: Statement of account amended, when.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 512 Appeals and Appellate Procedure

norms.text: In all cases of an application for trial de novo, the bill of items of the account sued on or filed as a counterclaim or setoff, or the statement of the plaintiff's cause of action, or of defendant's counterclaim or setoff, or other ground of defense filed before the associate circuit judge, may be amended upon a trial de novo to supply any deficiency or omission therein, when by such amendment substantial justice will be promoted; but no new item or cause of action not embraced or intended to be included in the original account or statement shall be added by such amendment. Such amendment shall be allowed upon such terms as to costs as the court may deem just and proper.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 633 renvoie, pour la recevabilité des prétentions nouvelles, aux règles applicables devant la juridiction dont la décision a été cassée. Les §§ 512.280, 512.290 et 512.300 encadrent pareillement les prétentions, demandes reconventionnelles et modifications nouvelles lors d’un trial de novo, mais dans ce cadre particulier.
correspondences.note_en: Article 633 subjects new claims to the rules applicable before the court whose decision was quashed. RSMo 512.280, 512.290, and 512.300 similarly regulate new claims, counterclaims, and amendments in a trial de novo, but only within that specific proceeding.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article limite la révision d’un compte aux corrections d’erreurs, omissions ou présentations inexactes. Le RSMo 512.300 permet, lors d’un nouveau procès, de modifier certains comptes pour remédier à une insuffisance ou omission, sans reprendre la même limitation générale.
correspondences.note_en: The article limits account review to correcting errors, omissions, or inaccurate presentation. RSMo 512.300 permits amendment of certain accounts on trial de novo to cure a deficiency or omission, but does not impose the same general limitation.

norms.heading: Procedure for trial de novo.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 512 Appeals and Appellate Procedure

norms.text: The trial de novo shall be governed by the practice in trials before circuit judges, except that by agreement of parties the case may be tried by a jury of not less than six persons.

norms.heading: Judgment against sureties, when.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 512 Appeals and Appellate Procedure

norms.text: In all cases of an application for trial de novo from an associate circuit judge, if on a trial anew, the judgment be against the applicant, such judgment shall be rendered against him or against him and his sureties in the recognizance for the application for trial de novo, if such recognizance be given.

norms.heading: Levy and real estate defined.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 513 Executions and Exemptions

norms.text:
1. The word "levy", as used in this chapter, shall be construed to mean the actual seizure of property by the officer charged with the execution of the writ.

2. The term "real estate" as used in this chapter shall be construed to include all estate and interest in lands, tenements and hereditaments, including a manufactured home as defined in section 700.010, which is real estate as defined in subsection 7 of section 442.015.

norms.heading: Executions, who may have.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 513 Executions and Exemptions

norms.text: The party in whose favor any judgment, order or decree is rendered, may have an execution in conformity therewith.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 501 lie l’exécution au passage en force de chose jugée, sous réserve du délai de grâce et de l’exécution provisoire. La Rule 81.09 organise la suspension de l’exécution pendant l’appel; les §§ 513.015 et 513.020 autorisent et limitent dans le temps les exécutions, sans poser la même condition générale de finalité.
correspondences.note_en: Article 501 makes a judgment executable upon finality, subject to a grace period or provisional enforcement. Rule 81.09 governs stays during appeal, while §§ 513.015 and 513.020 authorize and time-limit executions, but do not impose the same general finality condition.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article exige, en principe, une expédition revêtue de la formule exécutoire pour mettre un jugement ou un acte à exécution. Le Missouri autorise l’exécution au profit de la partie gagnante et prévoit une demande d’exécution, mais ne reprend pas cette exigence formelle générale ; une copie certifiée est prévue pour certains jugements non pécuniaires.
correspondences.note_en: The article generally requires an enforceable certified copy bearing the enforcement clause before execution. Missouri allows the prevailing party to obtain execution and requires an application, while a certified copy is specified only for certain non-money judgments; it has no general equivalent to the enforcement-clause requirement.

correspondences.note_fr: Le demandeur mandaté pour indemniser est réputé créancier afin de poursuivre l'exécution forcée du jugement. Le RSMo 513.015 reconnaît au bénéficiaire du jugement le droit à l'exécution, et la Rule 76.01 en règle la demande, mais aucun texte ne prévoit cette qualité spéciale du représentant mandaté.
correspondences.note_en: The indemnity-mandated claimant is deemed a judgment creditor for purposes of enforcing the judgment. RSMo 513.015 grants execution to the party in whose favor judgment was rendered, and Rule 76.01 governs the application, but neither addresses the special status of a mandated representative.

correspondences.note_fr: Les textes du Missouri régissent l’exécution des jugements, ordres ou décrets, mais ne prévoient pas directement que les extraits du procès-verbal d’une conciliation menée par le juge valent titre exécutoire.
correspondences.note_en: The Missouri provisions govern enforcement of judgments, orders, or decrees, but do not directly provide that extracts from minutes of a judge-led conciliation constitute enforceable titles.

norms.heading: Executions may issue, when.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 513 Executions and Exemptions

norms.text: Executions may issue upon a judgment at any time within ten years after the rendition of such judgment.
revisor_notes: Execution from probate court on judgment against plaintiff on claim against estate, RSMo 473.410

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 501 lie l’exécution au passage en force de chose jugée, sous réserve du délai de grâce et de l’exécution provisoire. La Rule 81.09 organise la suspension de l’exécution pendant l’appel; les §§ 513.015 et 513.020 autorisent et limitent dans le temps les exécutions, sans poser la même condition générale de finalité.
correspondences.note_en: Article 501 makes a judgment executable upon finality, subject to a grace period or provisional enforcement. Rule 81.09 governs stays during appeal, while §§ 513.015 and 513.020 authorize and time-limit executions, but do not impose the same general finality condition.

norms.heading: General execution, form.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 513 Executions and Exemptions

norms.text:
Such execution shall be a fieri facias against the goods, chattels and real estate of the party against whom the judgment, order or decree is rendered, and shall be to the following effect:

The state of Missouri, to the sheriff of the county of ______:

Whereas, A B, on the ______ day of ______, in the year of our Lord two thousand* and ______, at our court, hath recovered against C D, the sum of ______, for debt (or damages, as the case may be), and also for the sum of ______ which to the said A B were adjudged for his damages, as well as by reason of detaining the said debt, as for his cost in that suit expended: These are, therefore, to command you, that of the goods and chattels and real estate of the said C D, you cause to be made the debt, damages and costs (or damages and costs), and that you have the same before the judge of said court, on the ______ day of ______, to satisfy the debt, damages and costs aforesaid (or damages alone and costs), and that you certify how you execute this writ.

Witness: E F, clerk of the said court, at ______, this ______ day of ______ in the year ______

E F, clerk.
revisor_notes: *Revisor's Note: The words "nineteen hundred" appear in original rolls. After the year 2000 and in accordance with section 3.060, the reference was changed to "two thousand" by the Revisor.

norms.heading: Executions, when returnable.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 513 Executions and Exemptions

norms.text: Every execution issued from any court of record shall be made returnable at the next succeeding term, unless the plaintiff, or person to whose use the suit was brought, shall otherwise direct; then it shall be the duty of the clerk issuing the same to make it returnable to the second succeeding term.

norms.heading: Executions, where directed and executed.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 513 Executions and Exemptions

norms.text: Executions issued upon any judgment, order or decree rendered in any court of record, may be directed to and executed in any county in this state; and executions may issue at the same time to different counties.
revisor_notes: Execution not to issue from court where transcript of judgment of another court of record is filed, 511.480

norms.heading: Directed to any sheriff in the state, when.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 513 Executions and Exemptions

norms.text: Any party entitled to an execution from a court of record may have it directed as provided in section 513.035, or, at his option, he may have it directed to any sheriff in the state of Missouri; and such execution may be levied, served and returned by any sheriff in this state to whom it may be delivered within the county of which he is sheriff, in like manner and with the same effect as if it had been specially directed to him; but if no property, or not sufficient property to satisfy such execution, can be found in such county, the sheriff, at the option of the plaintiff, may make thereon a return of his proceedings and deliver it to the plaintiff, his agent or attorney, who may deliver the same to the sheriff of any other county in this state, who may levy, serve and return the same, as if it had been directed to him.

norms.heading: Duties of clerks in issuing executions.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 513 Executions and Exemptions

norms.text: The clerk shall, before delivering any execution issued by the clerk, endorse thereon the debt, damages and costs, or damages and costs, to be recovered, and shall maintain in his office record, and enter therein an abstract of all executions issued out of his office, showing the date, the names of the parties, amount of debt, damages and costs, or damages and costs to what officer directed, when made returnable, the return, if any, and a reference to the location of the record wherein the judgment or decree whereon such execution issued is entered; and every such clerk shall, moreover, keep a regular index to such abstract of executions, indexed or arranged alphabetically, both by the name of the plaintiff and defendant therein.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 702 prévoit la délivrance par le greffier d’un titre exécutoire lorsque le montant liquidé n’apparaît pas dans l’expédition. La Rule 77.06 permet l’exécution pour les frais avant ou après le jugement définitif, et le RSMo 513.045 encadre l’énonciation des frais dans l’exécution, sans instituer exactement le même titre.
correspondences.note_en: Article 702 requires the clerk to issue an enforceable title when the taxed amount is absent from the judgment copy. Rule 77.06 permits execution for costs before or after final judgment, and RSMo 513.045 requires costs to be stated on the execution, but Missouri does not provide the same precise clerk-issued title mechanism.

norms.heading: Sheriffs and deputies to endorse on execution the time of receipt — rank of writs.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 513 Executions and Exemptions

norms.text: The several sheriffs and their deputies shall, upon the receipt of a writ of execution, without fee for doing the same, endorse thereon the day of the month and year when they receive the same. If two or more writs shall be delivered on the same day, against the same persons, they shall have equal rank, and be executed accordingly.

norms.heading: Employees and laborers preferred creditors.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 513 Executions and Exemptions

norms.text:
1. Hereafter when the property of any company, corporation, firm or person shall be seized upon by any process of any court of this state, or when their business shall be suspended by the action of creditors, or be put into the hands of a receiver or trustee, then in all such cases the debts owing to laborers or servants, which have accrued by reason of their labor or employment, to an amount not exceeding one hundred dollars to each employee, for work or labor performed within six months next preceding the seizure or transfer of such property, shall be considered and treated as preferred debts, and such laborers or employees shall be preferred creditors, and shall be first paid in full; and if there be not sufficient to pay them in full, then the same shall be paid to them pro rata, after paying costs.

2. Any such laborer or servant desiring to enforce his or her claim for wages under this section shall present a statement under oath showing the amount due after allowing all just credits and setoffs, the kind of work for which such wages are due, and when performed, to the officer, person or court charged with such property, within ten days after the seizure thereof on any execution or writ of attachment, or within thirty days after the same may have been placed in the hands of any receiver or trustee; and thereupon it shall be the duty of the person or court receiving such statement to pay the amount of such claim or claims to the person or persons entitled thereto, after first paying all costs occasioned by the seizure of such property, out of the proceeds of the sale of the property seized; provided, that any person interested may contest any such claim or claims, or any part thereof, by filing exceptions thereto, supported by affidavit, with the officer having the custody of such property; and thereupon the claimant shall be required to reduce his claim to judgment before some court having jurisdiction thereof before any part thereof shall be paid.

norms.heading: Limitation of actions for preference.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 513 Executions and Exemptions

norms.text: The persons specified in section 513.470, in order to secure the benefit thereof, shall commence their actions within six months next after the last services shall have been rendered.

norms.heading: Finding as to preferred amount recited in execution and judgment.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 513 Executions and Exemptions

norms.text: The court or jury trying such action shall, if they find for the plaintiff, also find how much he or she is entitled to recover for services, such as are specified in section 513.470, for which suit was commenced, within the time limited in section 513.060, which facts shall be set forth in the judgment rendered, and recited in the execution issued thereon.

norms.heading: Execution against heir to be special.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 513 Executions and Exemptions

norms.text: When execution shall be issued against any person, as heir or devisee, the officer to whom the same shall be directed, shall be commanded only that of the goods and chattels which were of the ancestor or testator at the time of his death, he cause to be made the debt, damages and costs; and if sufficient goods and chattels cannot be found in his county, then that of the real estate which was of the ancestor or testator at the time of his death, he cause to be made the debt, damages and costs or sum of money in such execution specified.

norms.heading: Execution against executors or administrators prohibited.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 513 Executions and Exemptions

norms.text: No execution shall issue upon any judgment or decree rendered against the testator or intestate in his lifetime, or against his executors or administrators after his death, which judgment or decree constitutes a demand against the estate of any testator or intestate, within the meaning of the statute respecting executors and administrators; but all such demands shall be classed and proceeded on in the court having probate jurisdiction, as required by said statute.

norms.heading: Execution sued out by administrator de bonis non.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 513 Executions and Exemptions

norms.text: Where a judgment shall have been or may hereafter be had in the name of an executor or administrator, execution thereafter may be sued out or an action thereon maintained by the administrator de bonis non, upon his filing in the clerk's office of the court in which such judgment was rendered a certified copy of his letters of administration de bonis non.

norms.heading: Execution to be lien, when.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 513 Executions and Exemptions

norms.text: No execution prior to the levy thereof shall be a lien on any goods, chattels or other personal property, or the rights or shares in any stock, or any real estate to which the lien of the judgment, order or decree does not extend; and whenever an execution shall be levied upon real estate, not then charged with the lien of the judgment, order or decree upon which such execution issued, it shall be the duty of the officer making such levy immediately to file with the recorder of deeds of the city or county in which such real estate is situated a notice of such levy, showing the date and style of the execution, the date of levy, the amount of the debt and costs, and a description of the real estate levied upon, which shall be recorded and indexed in a separate volume by the recorder, in the same manner that deeds to real estate are required to be recorded and indexed in a separate volume, and the recording fee therefor shall be charged and collected as other costs; and the failure of said officer to file said notice, as required by this chapter, shall be a breach of his official bond, and any person injured by the failure of the sheriff to file said notice shall have a right of action on said bond.

norms.heading: Property which may be sold under attachment and execution.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 513 Executions and Exemptions

norms.heading: Defendant may elect what property shall be sold.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 513 Executions and Exemptions
